### Item 148 (2026-09-12)

**Item 147 seeded the cover and left it unspendable, and not only for the reason
it named.**  That item said the missing piece was a field on
`ImplicitKeyPack` — true, and this item adds it — but the field alone would not
have been enough, because two of item 147's own readings were wrong for the
consumer that has to spend them.  Both were found by trying to pay, and both are
machine-checked here.

**The bound was the wrong one.**  `pendingMapValue.h_frames` bounded the floor by
the park's own index (`lo ≤ n`).  The landing that SPENDS a cover stands BELOW
that index — that is what a dedent is — and
`preprocess_landing_mem_or_seq` takes `lo ≤ s_prep.col` as a premise — asked
BEFORE the landing's membership is known, since membership is what the lemma
derives.  So the bound has to reach below the landing without naming it, and
`lo ≤ n` does not.  A bound over the WIDTHS does: it drags the floor down to the
outermost width the frames name, and in a chain rooted at column 0 that pins it
AT 0, where the premise is free for any landing whatever (the lemma's own
docstring: "at `lo = 0` the hypothesis is free").  Bounding by the widths alone
fails the other way: where the frames are empty it says nothing, and a floor
free to climb weakens the cover to vacuity (`Covered.raise_floor`).
`IndentStackCover.Floor lo n ks` is both halves —

```
lo ≤ n ∧ ∀ k' ∈ ks, lo ≤ k'
```

— and the guard proves each half is what the other cannot supply: a
counterexample showing the second does not follow from the first
(`lo = n = 2`, `ks = [1]`), and a vacuous witness showing the first does not
follow from the second.  Item 147's DOCS entry is struck and corrected in place.

**And the list was the wrong one.**  The cover a pack carries is over `k :: ks`,
the key's OWN level included, not over `ks`.  The two branches that pay reach it
from opposite sides: a key NESTED below the park opens its level at the `:`
still to come, so its width is free (`Covered.cons`); a key that LANDED on an
open level finds that level already on the scanner's stack and cannot drop it.
Stating the full list is what lets one field serve both, and it is what makes
the `:`'s own push a no-op on the cover — the level it opens is already a frame,
the step names it twice, and `Covered.dedup_head` folds it back.

**The transport is the `:` and nothing else.**  Between a park and the next park
lie a content dispatch (the key) and a `:` dispatch (the value indicator), each
with its own preprocessing.  Preprocessing only pops (`preprocess_cover`) and a
content dispatch writes no level (`dispatchContent_cover`), so the whole of the
carriage is `scanValuePrepare`.  `scanValuePrepare_cover` reports the level it
opens with an EXISTENTIAL, which is all a step-generic caller can say; a caller
holding the live key holds its column, and that is the difference between
`c :: ks` for an unknown `c` and the `k :: ks` the frames already name.  The
named form takes the key-or-`?`-line arm as its premise — which is exactly what
rules out `[196]`'s keyless push at the cursor — and
`scanValueClearKey_arm` supplies it whichever way the clear goes.

**What pays.**  The two root `:`/`?` producers seed, as in item 147, now on both
frame faces — `h_closeF` needs the cover as much as `h_frames`, because the key
dispatch's NESTED branch reads the one and its DEDENT branch the other, and two
existentials cannot be identified after the fact.  The NESTED branch of both key
dispatch lemmas pays the pack: the landed key's width joins the caller's frames
for free and the floor stays strictly left of it (`n < w` on that branch).  Both
implicit `:` producers spend the pack into the next park's two faces.  **So the
chain closes**: every hop is discharged, and none of the payments is conditional
on anything the accumulation cannot supply, so a cover seeded at a root is
carried through every nested implicit key on the way down — which is what the
field was for.

**What does not pay, and why it is not an unthreaded premise.**  The DEDENT
branch does not.  The level the landing popped TO is still on the scanner's
stack, so the pack's cover there is over `w :: ks'` while the caller's is over
the whole of `ks` — and `ResumeFrames.resumeAt` drops every width above `w`.

sublist is the half the FLOOR spends, and the half the COVER spends is the
opposite direction, COMPLETENESS, that nothing below the landing was dropped.
None of the three is at that branch.  A
fresh document's root, a SEQUENCE park and the flow OPEN pay `Or.inr trivial`
for a different reason: they have no carried stack to inherit, and the chain is
seeded at the `:`/`?` producers, which is where `Mono` rides.

### Item 149 (2026-09-12)

**The dedent landing spends the cover.**  Item 148 carried a cover from a root
down an unbounded chain of nested implicit keys and left ONE branch punting:
`entryKeyPack_of_dispatch`'s dedent, where the landing pops to a level below the
park's own.  That branch now pays, and so does its props twin.

**The obstacle was real and the reading of it was one half short.**  Item 148
named three things the branch would need — the stack's SHAPE in the content
lane, the landing's own floor, and `resumeAt`'s widths *as a sublist of the ones
it popped from*.  The first two stand.  The third names one of the two halves,
and not the one that was missing.  A sublist is exactly what the FLOOR spends —
`Floor.pop_to`: every surviving width was a frame the park had already bounded,
so the bound travels without being re-measured.  What the COVER spends is the
other direction, completeness: given a level the scanner still holds strictly
below the landing, is it still one of the frames?  A sublist cannot answer that
(`[]` is a sublist of every list), so on item 148's reading the branch would
have paid the floor and stalled at the cover.
`ResumeWidths ks ks' j := ∀ k', k' ∈ ks' ↔ (k' ∈ ks ∧ k' < j)` states what the
popped list IS, and both halves fall out of `ResumeFrames.resumeAt`'s own
recursion with no new premise: the strict decrease each `level` constructor
carries is visited at exactly the steps the pop descends through.  Item 148's
text is struck and corrected where it stands, and the three readings are
machine-checked side by side in the new guard's §1 — `[]` satisfies the bound
`∀ k' ∈ ks', k' < 2`, `[]` is a sublist of `[4, 2, 0]`, and
`¬ ResumeWidths [4, 2, 0] [] 2`.

**What reads one list as the other is the landing's floor, not a list fact.**
The park's cover is over the whole of `ks`; the pack the landing opens carries
`w :: ks'`, and `ks'` holds none of the levels above `w`.  Those levels are not
dropped from the cover by fiat — preprocessing's unwind POPPED them, so the
stack the dispatch receives has nothing above `w` left to name.  That is a
statement about the TOP, and `Mono` is what turns it into one about every entry:
`IndentStackCover.Covered.pop_to`.  The frames' own bound does not move at all
(`Floor.pop_to`): `w` is one of the widths the park already bounded, and so is
every width the landing keeps.

**Which half of `Floor` pays here is worth recording.**  `Floor.pop_to` reads
the WIDTHS half (`∀ k' ∈ ks, lo ≤ k'`) twice and the index half (`lo ≤ n`) not
at all — so the conjunct item 148 ADDED is the whole of what the dedent spends,
and the conjunct it inherited from item 147 is spent at the NESTED branch
instead (`Floor.mono_index`).  The two branches of the key dispatch are what
make both halves live, which is the same reason `h_closeF` and `h_frames` both
have to carry a cover.

**`Mono` is load-bearing, and the guard says so by refuting the lemma without

### Item 150 (2026-09-12)

**The value-line stack carries its cover.**  Items 147–149 gave the STREAM lane
a cover and taught the dedent landing to spend it.  The value-line lane — the
frames an open `[186]` explicit key leaves standing, bottomed at the `?`'s own
unpaid value line rather than at the finished stream — carried none, on either
face, and item 149 listed it as the next thing that could pay.  It does now, at
both pack lemmas, with item 149's `dedent_cover_of_landing` called verbatim.

**One thing does not mirror, and it is the floor's index.**  The stream faces
bottom at the stream and carry `Floor lo n ks`.  These bottom at the `?`, whose
own level is deliberately NOT one of their frames — resuming there is the
entry's unpaid value line, not a sibling — so a cover over them cannot stand at
the park's own floor.  At the seed it is `ks = []` and the `?` has just pushed a
mapping level at `k`: `Covered k []` would have to fail to name it, and does.
One column above it is true, and it is not a vacuity — it says the push left
nothing at or right of `k + 1`.  So these faces carry `Floor lo (n + 1) ks`,
`IndentStackCover.covered_nil_of_top_le` is the seed, and a floor stated at `n`
would have been payable by nobody.  All four readings are machine-checked side
by side in the new guard's §1, the seed's `Mono` premise refuted on item 149's
own `[-1, 5, 1]` stack.

**The rest of the lane is item 148's shape and item 149's lemma.**  The chain's
hop climbs the index by one (`Floor.mono_index (Nat.le_succ k)`) and leaves the
floor where the producer put it; the nested branch conses the landed width, `n <
w` carrying `lo ≤ n + 1 ≤ w`; the dedent branch calls
`dedent_cover_of_landing`, which reads `Floor`'s WIDTHS half and never its
index — which is exactly why the lane's higher index rides through it with no
new lemma at all.  The two lanes' lists stay independent: the membership test
and the payment are both taken twice, because a landing width can name a level
in one stack and not the other.

**The seed came off a measurement already being taken.**
`indicator_cover_at_col` proved the top's bound and then read it ONE way;  it
now names the top and reads it twice, so the `?` producer's value-line payment
costs the walk nothing.  `question_open_map` gains the second reading as a
premise (`h_cov_nil`), and `colon_open_map` — a `[189]` empty-key entry, with no
explicit frame over it — keeps the `Or.inr trivial` it already paid.

**The price, measured.**  **ONE** new declaration, `covered_nil_of_top_le`, and
the stats bear that out exactly: proofs, library and env each move by **+1**.
One conclusion is widened (`indicator_cover_at_col`, now a pair), one premise
added (`question_open_map.h_cov_nil`), and **16** field shapes gain the cover
conjunct — **10** at `n + 1` (the park's two faces, the four pack-lemma premises
and the four relay faces) and **6** at the pack's own index (`ImplicitKeyPack`,
`PropsKeyPack`, both `colon_open_map` route faces and `content_dispatch_routed`'s
two).  Nine destructurings widen to match, three covers step across
preprocessing's pops beside the stream twin already doing it, and three places
punt where there is no slot to punt into: the flow twin at
`flowKeyPack_of_close`, the props close that drops back to it, and
`resumectx_of_landing` — which has no cover slot on EITHER lane, so the value
face is projected there exactly as item 149 left the stream face.  **613**
insertions, **64** deletions, one new guard file.

**Item 149's own forecast was wrong about what comes next, and the correction is
one line of Lean.**  It named the membership split — `by_cases hmem : w ∈ ks`,
which `preprocess_landing_mem_or_seq` would derive — as the only punt left about
the landing rather than the caller.  `KeyPackPunt.dedent` takes no argument, so
the punt disjunct is inhabited at every state; the branch therefore already
returns the pack at exactly the inputs where `w ∈ ks` holds, and deriving that
membership from the cover cannot add one input to that set.  It can only
re-prove what a total case split has already decided.  What would move the
domain is the opposite change — a PAYLOAD on the constructor, so a consumer
holding the cover refutes the punt — which is the shape `tab` and
`implicitValue` already have and `noFrame` had before it was deleted.  There is
also a fourth requirement item 149's list did not name: the derivation wants the
landing at or right of the cover's FLOOR, and a dedent lands strictly left of
the park's index, where `Floor`'s index half says nothing.  Both are
machine-checked in the new guard's §5 (`example (s : ScannerState) :
KeyPackPunt s := KeyPackPunt.dedent`, and a counterexample to
`Floor lo n ks → w < n → lo ≤ w`), and item 149's DOCS and guard are struck and
corrected where they stand.

**And item 149's axiom sentence was incomplete.**  It said the only non-standard
axioms anywhere downstream are the `native_decide` ones from `ScalarProduction`'s
plain-scalar lemmas and `StructureProduction`'s anchor-name loop.
`dispatchBlockKey_full_prod` and `dispatchBlockValue_full_prod` — in
`StreamAccum` itself, and present at `9616c45f` — each carry two more, and they
appear in `question_open_map` and both `colon_open_map` openers.  None is new;
the sentence was.  Struck in place.

### Item 151 (2026-09-12)

**The resuming key context carries the landing's cover.**  Items 149 and 150

— had no slot for a cover on either lane.  So the one relay that holds BOTH of
the stack's readings, `accum_content_on_pendingMapValue_indented`'s dedent,
projected both of them away on the way in.  This item gives the context a slot
on each lane, pays them at that relay, and spends them into the two pack fields
`content_dispatch_routed` builds.

**The context's floor index is the PACK's, on both lanes — which is where the
value lane stops mirroring its parks.**  A park's value-line frames exclude the
`?`'s own level, so their cover stands one column above the park (item 150).
The key THIS landing heads is a mapping level of either stack, so nothing is
excluded here: `Floor lo k (k :: ks)` is what both faces carry, the same shape
the pack field takes.  The guard's §1 checks the discrimination on a three-entry
stack — a `?` at 0 with a key at 2 — where `Covered 1 []` is FALSE (the key's
level is open and unnamed) and `Covered 1 [2]` is true.

**The index on the way IN is forgotten, and that is what makes one payer serve
both lanes.**  The incoming faces are bounded at different indices by
construction — `n` on the stream lane, `n + 1` on the value lane — and the hop
reads neither of them: `IndentStackCover.Floor.pop_to` spends the WIDTHS half
alone.  So both faces hand the payer `∃ lo n, Floor lo n ks ∧ Covered lo ks sc`,

**The one new declaration is a factoring, not an addition.**
`dedent_cover_of_floor` is the arithmetic item 149's `dedent_cover_of_landing`
performs, with that lemma's two escapes taken OUT of it — a caller that cannot
measure its stack, and a park at a line start whose walk armed no unwind.  Both

them wants the payment and not a disjunction to case on.  `dedent_cover_of_landing`
now calls it, so the hop is authored once; and the new lemma's conclusion is a
plain `∃`, which is the interrogability this item actually buys — a consumer can
tell that it was paid, where `∨ True` can never be interrogated after the fact.

**Where the payment stands, and why it is reachable there.**  The relay's park

input `landing_floor_of_arm` wants.  The other disjunct is the step that stayed
on the line, which this landing is not; refuting it costs more than the punt it
would replace, so it punts.

**§4 measures the lane, and the measure discriminates.**  Item 99's own dedent

### Item 154 (2026-09-13)

**The column-0 landing pays, off the park's own indent check.**  Item 152 gave
`pendingContent`'s two frames fields a cover and spent it at
`accum_content_pending`'s landing skeleton — but not on every landing.  The
skeleton splits on the park's column, and the COLUMN-0 arm punted its PAYER.

park down to column 0, and a park already AT a line start crosses no such walk.
Item 152 recorded it as item 147's escape "at the consumer instead of at a
producer"; item 153 recorded it as one of two remaining entries.  This is that
entry.

**The floor is not the walk's.**  It is preprocessing's UNWIND, and outside a
flow the unwind runs on exactly one condition: `needIndentCheck`.  A park that
reached column 0 got there by consuming a break, and every break arms the flag.
So the datum the arm needs is the PARK's, not the landing's — which is item 77's
own division of labor (`landing_or_park_save`: the landing pays for a park off a
line start, the park's flag pays for one at it), one field over.
`pendingContent` gains `h_nic0 : (sp_scan.col = 0 → sc.needIndentCheck = true) ∨
True`, and both column-0 landings spend it through the same `have`.

**The escape is measured, not assumed — and it is what fixes the field's
shape.**  A block-scalar header at end of input consumes no break:
`scanBlockScalarConsumeNewline`'s `!hasMore` arm skips it, and `"k: |"` really
does stop with the flag DOWN.  So the unconditional claim is FALSE.  That same
header never left its line, so it stops at column 4 — strictly right of 0 —
which is why the field is stated as an implication FROM column 0: **the one
shape that cannot pay is the one shape that cannot reach the premise.**  Had the
lemma been stated unconditionally it would simply have failed to prove; stating
it against the measurement got the shape right first.

**Producer census, established by the compiler.**  The same payment term was
attempted at all **14** `pendingContent` producers and kept where it typechecks:

from its own `dispatchContent_blockScalar_prod`; **8 punt** — the other content
arms, which have no `hbs`; **2 punt** — the flow CLOSES, which run no content
dispatch at all.  The punts are free in the strong sense: they name a premise
none of their parks can satisfy.  That is the claim the sweep below carries.

### Item 155 (2026-09-13)

**The sequence lane gets frames, and then a cover.**  Items 152 and 153 left one
entry on the menu: `pendingProps.h_closeFE`, `pendingBlockContent.h_closeF` and
`pendingBlock.h_closeF`, "one chain carrying widths alone", with the sequence
park's relay owing a `Mono` and a `SentinelBase` besides.  This is that entry —
and measuring it first showed the entry was **mis-stated**.

**A cover over an empty list is spendable nowhere.**  The landing's hop is
`ResumeFrames.resumeAt`, whose premise is `j ∈ ks`: a landing resumes only at a
width the frames NAME.  Flipping `pendingBlock.h_closeF`'s escape from `True` to
`False` reports **six punts of seven producers**, and the seventh —
`accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`'s landed `-` — pays `ks = []`.  So the lane's
frames were empty wherever they existed at all, and the three fields' missing
cover was never the residue.  The FRAMES were.

**Where a non-empty list exists is the mapping value the sequence fills.**  A
landed `-` on a `pendingMapValue` opens the collection that becomes the awaited
node, and the mapping level the park stands in is still open underneath it —
which is what that park's `h_closeF` has said since item 108, cover included.
`accum_block_on_closeThenBlock` closes the park before its `-` arm runs, so the
item carries that reading past the close as `h_valF`, and the sequence park's
frames become `nv :: ks`.  `k:⏎␣␣- a⏎b: 2` now resumes the mapping the sequence
was written inside instead of re-opening at the root.

**The side condition is `[183]`'s `m` read as a bound**, and its failing case
cannot arise.  `nestedBlockSeq` wants `nv ≤ k` and the frames are strictly
decreasing, so the payment runs at `nv < k` and keeps item 99's bottomed reading
otherwise.  The shape that fails it is `seq-spaces` — a sequence at its key's own
column (`k:⏎- a`) — and there the `-` pushes NO level: the stack stays `[0M]` and
the state never has the shape the payment asks about.  **The one shape that
cannot pay is the one shape that cannot reach the premise**, which is item 154's
finding at a different field.

**Census, by the compiler.**  `h_valF` flipped to `∨ False` distinguishes its
callers by the argument each error names: **9 punts** (`trivial`) and **2
payers** (`h_closeF155`), the two branches of `accum_block_pending`'s
`pendingMapValue` arm — the only park that awaits a node when a block indicator
lands on it.  Flipping the cover conjunct on both the field and the local that
pays it gives **exactly two errors, and they are the two `ks = []` fallbacks**:
the cover is present precisely where the frames are non-empty.

**The floor is bounded at the field's own index, and that buys one more hop.**
Items 152/153 left the index existential because their payers bounded their lists
at levels the consumer could not name.  This lane's payer knows its index (`nv <
k` gives it), so the three fields state `Floor lo n ks` rather than `∃ m, Floor

closing **six** punts at the entry-key-pack relays (items 148 and 149, three

whole.  What was missing was never the reasoning — it was the two stack readings

**The chain is the token array's own, and every link is now a lemma.**  Off `&`

scalar's arm proved separately as `scanBlockScalar_tokens_push` — the value arms

own last REAL slot as its predecessor (`trailingNodeRun?_push_body`, the dual of
`trailingNodeRun?_push_none`, over `prevRealIdx?_push` and `prevRealIdx?_lt`).
A completed node tail offers that run no slot, because `completesFlowValue` and
`offersNodeSlot` are disjoint (`CompletedTail.danglingPred`).  So the park reads

open level — `danglingPark_of_dispatch` — and that is
`danglingNodePos?`'s four conditions in order.  Spent against the two §9.2
checks it is `danglingPark_refutes_landing` and `danglingPark_refutes_eof`.

**The predecessor is stated as a `prevRealIdx?` fact, not as `CompletedTail`,
and that is not a generalization for its own sake.**  Preprocessing's unwind
EMITS `blockEnd` before the dispatch runs, so at a landing that popped the
array's last real token is a `blockEnd` rather than the park's own tail — and a
`blockEnd` offers no slot either.  Stating the premise at the reading the lemma
actually spends leaves that transport available; stating it as `CompletedTail`
would have closed the popping half out by construction.

`:`, which are `YamlToken.offersNodeSlot`'s own members, so the content FILLS a
slot and there is no dangling run at all; the props park stands at the

### Item 157 (2026-09-13)

**The park's face, built and spent — and item 156's named obstacle was not
one.**  Item 141 named the face and priced it at 32 sites; item 156 derived the
reading the producer has to hand over and left the consumer side unnamed.  This
item builds the consumer side, threads it through the accumulation, and spends
it: at a content landing off a completed node, the bare-document reading now has
no input to serve at all.

**The face, as it landed.**  `pendingContent.h_closable` and
`PendingNode.close_with_ssl` take `danglingNodePos? sc = none` as a PREMISE —
a park whose completed node is a §9.2-dangling run has no `[211]` reading, so
the close is offered only to a consumer that can say the landing already refused
one.  Two readings pay it and they are §9.2's own two checks:
`dangling_none_of_check` at a landing that crossed a break (gated on
`simpleKeyAllowed`) and `dangling_none_of_eof` at end of input (gated on
nothing).  `h_dn` is threaded from `scanNextToken_accum_step` — where item 141
measured it was already derived and discarded — to all four dispatchers, and
from `scanLoop_grammar_prod`'s EOF branch to `eof_pending`.

The face itself is **32 sites in 9 holders, in ONE wave**, exactly the price item
156 measured.  Beside it the THREADING, which item 156 did not price: `h_dn`
becomes a parameter of **18** declarations, and the premise-carrying close
(`danglingNodePos? sc = none → ∀ sp_mid, …`) appears in **10** plus the
`pendingContent` constructor.  No declaration was deleted and no proof rewired.

**The transport is the item's one new piece of mathematics.**  The reading is
taken at the PARK's state and the route is refuted at the LANDING's, one
preprocessing later, and preprocessing has two writers that touch the token
array: the save, which reserves two placeholders, and the unwind, which emits
`blockEnd`.  `CompletedTail` does NOT survive the second one — a `blockEnd`
completes no value — which is why item 156 stated the producer's premise as a
`prevRealIdx?` fact instead.  `DanglingPred` (the premise, named) does survive:
`prevRealIdx?` walks past placeholders by construction, and a `blockEnd` offers
the coming run no slot either.  `preprocess_danglingPred` is that transport, over
`unwindIndentsLoop_tokens_shape` and `saveSimpleKey_tokens_shape` — the two
shapes each writer can leave the array in — and the popping half is not
hypothetical: at `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎b: 2`, an ACCEPTED input, the park's last real token
completes a value and the landing's is the `blockEnd` the unwind emitted.

**What the face buys.**  Item 139 halved `bareNodeRoute`'s domain at the content
landing by refuting the landing that stands at NO open level.  The other half —
the landing that rests ON one — is the DANGLING one, and the check that refuses
it cannot see the run until it is scanned.  `danglingPark_refutes_route` closes
that gap: the park the dispatch makes reads `some` (item 156), the consumer that
closes it hands back `none`, and the two cannot both hold.  So for a park that
finished a node and a landing that completes a value **both halves of the
discriminator are now refuted, with no case split on the stack left over**.

`bareNodeRoute_or_refused_content` carries it, gated by `ContentRouteGate`
because `content_dispatch_routed`'s two consumers are not alike: a
value-completing character parks as `pendingContent` and refutes; a `&`/`!`
parks as `pendingProps`, which has no face, and there the route stands.  The
gate is therefore not a wart — it NAMES the residue.

| site | form | what is left of its domain |
|---|---|---|
| `accum_content_pending` ×2 (content landing) | `bareNodeRoute_or_refused_content` | the `&`/`!` gate, and parks with no completed tail |
| `accum_block_on_closeThenBlock` (block landing) | `bareNodeRoute_or_refused` | item 139's `h_op = true` half, whole |
| `content_dispatch_after_close` (row 19's 1c) | `bareNodeRoute` | a ROUTE, not a refutation (item 156) |

**Item 156's named obstacle was not an obstacle, and this is our own record
being wrong.**  Item 156 recorded `accum_block_pending` as the face's one
obstacle and named two repairs — move its `h_close_pending` into the arms that
spend it, or stop `accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`'s `:` fallback taking an

inside `h_close_pending`'s own type, so the `have` before the case split costs
nothing and the premise is discharged where the close is SPENT — and

Item 141's punting witness `a: &x 1⏎*x : 2` takes the NO-BREAK arm, which spends

CONCLUSION must be discharged wherever the conclusion is used) and empty about
the shape item 156 chose; item 156 re-confirmed the wall without re-measuring it
against its own shape.  Both records are struck in place.

**The gating asymmetry, measured rather than argued.**  Five landings, each read
at the state its park stands in:

| input | landing | `simpleKeyAllowed` | the park reads | the check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎b: 2` | `:` | false | `some 2,0` | stands aside |
| `a: 1⏎b: 2` | `:` | false | `some 1,0` | stands aside |
| `a: &x 1⏎*x : 2` | `:` | false | `some 1,0` | stands aside |

The three flag-down rows are accepted inputs, and they are exactly the landings

### Item 158 (2026-09-13)

**The property lane's reading, derived — and the half of it that scans clean.**
Item 157 named `pendingProps` as the gate's residue and recorded the lane as one
item, on the strength of four witnesses the scanner refuses.  This item lands the
producer half, takes the character premises off everything item 156 built, and
measures that claim — which is **half true**.  The half that is not is why the
field item 157 named cannot simply be added, and it was found by running the
lane rather than by reading it.

**The dispatcher's token census, in ONE statement.**
`dispatchContent_tokens_push_prop` says a `&` pushes one `.anchor` and a `!` one
`.tag`, at the dispatch's own `currentPos`; `dispatchContent_tokens_push_node`
puts it beside item 156's body arm, and there is no third arm.
`trailingNodeRun?_push_prop` is `trailingNodeRun?`'s property arm — a property
pushed on top starts a trailing run of ONE with the array's own last real slot as
its predecessor, exactly as a body does.  So `danglingPark_of_dispatch` and its
three spent forms lose their `c ≠ '&'` and `c ≠ '!'` premises, and
`ContentRouteGate`'s LEFT disjunct loses them with it:

```
before:  (c ≠ '&' ∧ c ≠ '!' ∧ danglingNodePos? s' = none) ∨ (c = '&' ∨ c = '!')
after:                        danglingNodePos? s' = none  ∨ (c = '&' ∨ c = '!')
```

What the right disjunct names is therefore no longer "the two property
characters" but the STATE they park in.  The refutation is character-uniform
now — given the reading, a `&` landing on an open level behind a completed node
is refuted exactly as a scalar one is — and what is missing at `&`/`!` is a
FIELD.

**The lane splits, and item 157's four witnesses are one half of it.**  All four
are BLOCK-bodied, and all four are refused at the RUN's start, which is the
property:

| shape | scanner | parser |
|---|---|---|
| `a: 1⏎&p b`, `k:⏎␣␣a: 1⏎␣␣&p b`, `- a⏎&p b`, `a: 1⏎!!str b` | refused at the run's start | same position |
| `a: 1⏎&p [b]`, `a: 1⏎&p {b: 1}`, `a: 1⏎!t [b]`, `- a⏎&p [b]` | **SCAN-OK** | refused at `1,0` |
| `a: 1⏎[b]` (no run) | refused — §8.1's floor | same position |

Two mechanisms miss the flow-bodied half and they miss it for different reasons.
§9.2's end-of-input check reads `trailingNodeRun?`, and a `]` is neither a body
nor a property — so once the collection closes the array ends in no node run at
all: at `a: 1⏎&p [b]` the props park reads `some 1,0` and the very next step, the
`[`, reads `none`.  And §8.1's floor, which refuses the same shape WITHOUT a run,
measures the BRACKET's column — which the property run has moved right.

**So the props park really does owe an unconditional route**, and the face item
157 named cannot be a premise on `pendingProps.h_route` as it stands.  The route
has three consumers: `PendingNode.close_with_ssl` would pay from item 157's own
`h_nd` for free; `accum_content_pending` would pay from the next park's premise
one push later; `accum_flow_open_depth0` is the flow ride above and can pay
nothing, because the input it serves is live.

**The second consumer has its own obstacle, and it is about the token array.**  A
property run's reading transports across a BODY push — the walk-back reaches the
same run start — but not across a PROPERTY push, because the start MOVES.
`trailingNodeRun?` walks back over properties with no line filter, while
`trailingPropertyRunOnLine` (which the `[96]` guards read) has one, so a run may
span a break: at `&a⏎!t &b x` — **SCAN-OK**, parser-refused at `1,3` — the token
run starts at the `&a` on line 0 until the third property pushes the start down
to the `!t` on line 1.  The same three properties on one line are refused
(`invalidNodeProperties '&' 0 6`), so the shape exists only because of the break.
A premise stated as `danglingNodePos? sc = none` therefore does not relay through
the run's own extension, which is what the next item has to solve.

`danglingNodePos? sc = none` — the face `pendingContent` has carried since item
157 and `pendingBlockContent` since item 159 — and building `StreamAccum` names

| class | sites | pays with |
|---|---|---|
| `PendingNode.close_with_ssl` | 1 | `h_nd`, its own parameter |
| the landing producers (`content_dispatch_routed` and its four siblings) | 10 | the gate itself, once the right disjunct is gone |

**The relay, in three pushes.**  A `[96]` park's own last token is a property,
so every push onto it is the case item 158's two push lemmas EXCLUDE
(`hprop : ts[i]!.val.isNodeProperty = false`), and the three that can happen do
three different things:

| push | the reading | lemma |
|---|---|---|
| a node BODY | PRESERVED — the walk-back crosses the property and reaches the same start | `trailingNodeRun?_push_body_onProp`, and `danglingNodePos?_dispatch_body_onProp` at the state |
| a `[96]` PROPERTY | the start MOVES to the park's own last token | `trailingNodeRun?_push_prop_onProp`, `trailingNodeRun?_dispatch_prop_onProp` |
| a flow COLLECTION | PRESERVED, read at its CLOSE | `trailingNodeRun?_flowClose_reads_park` |

So the run's ride into its own content carries §9.2's verdict unchanged, and the
run's EXTENSION does not: `&a⏎!t &b x` leaves the `&a` on line 0 for the `!t` on
line 1, which is `PropsParkDangling` §4's witness with a lemma under it at last.
Under all three sit `trailingNodeRun?_bounds` — every arm reports a start inside
the array with `prevRealIdx?` of it as the predecessor — and
`danglingNodePos?_congr`, which says the verdict depends on the trailing RUN and
not on the array.  That pair is what lets a reading be transported by an
agreement on a PREFIX, which is what all three pushes are.

**The third is item 159's arm, measured end to end.**  `a: 1⏎&p [b]` reads
`1,0` at the park after `&p`, reads NOTHING inside the collection (in flow), and
reads `1,0` again at the `]`.  The lemma takes the walk's own answer as a
HYPOTHESIS (`flowOpenIdx? a i = some b.size`) because finding the open is a fact
about the token array's bracket BALANCE — and the balance is what
`FlowOpenStack`'s kinds array already indexes.

There is no scanner state in it, so a guard on `h_route` cannot be discharged

| shape | scanner | which half |
|---|---|---|
| `a: 1⏎&p [b]: c` | SCAN-OK, PARSE-OK | the collection heads an implicit KEY — `resume.key` |
| `a: 1⏎&p [b]` | `invalidBareDocument 1,0` | the collection closes as a VALUE — `resume.value` |

So `resume.value`'s domain at a dangling park holds no accepted input, the
refusal that empties it is read at the CLOSE, and by the third measurement above

`FlowBaseRoutes.value`**, one hypothesis away.

### Item 161 (2026-09-13)

**The bracket balance, read FORWARD — and the gate priced to its ten sites.**
Item 160 left the property lane one hypothesis short: `FlowBaseRoutes.value` is
where the gate belongs, and putting it there needs
`trailingNodeRun?_flowClose_reads_park`, which holds its own answer as a
premise — `flowOpenIdx? s_cl.tokens i = some s_park.tokens.size`, "the close
finds ITS open".  This item supplies it, and the shape it is supplied in is the
whole point.

**A backward walk is not a step invariant.**  `flowOpenIdx?` reads the token
array BACKWARD from the close, counting closes it has yet to balance.  Nothing
an accumulation carries can maintain that: it is a fact about a finished array,
re-derived from scratch at every reading, and there is no step at which it
"becomes" true.  The same balance read FORWARD is a STACK — `flowOpenIdxStack`,
the indices of the flow opens not yet closed in `ts[0, i)`, innermost first —
and a stack is maintained one push at a time.

`flowOpenIdxLoop_eq_stack` is that the two readings are the same reading, and
it holds at every depth at once: the backward walk with `d` closes outstanding
is the `d`-th element of the forward stack.  The three transports are then the
entire per-step cost — an open conses its own index, a close pops the innermost,
and **everything else is inert**, which is what carries a reading across the
placeholders a simple key reserves.  `FlowOpenHeld ts d o S` packages the one
shape a flow tower needs: the base frame's own open at index `o`, still held
under `d` nested ones.

**Where the depth index comes from, and where it does not.**  Not from the
scanner.  The accumulation already carries the tower's depth as `FlowStackB`'s
own index, and a base frame reads `d = 0` — so `FlowOpenHeld.flowOpenIdx?`
discharges item 160's premise from a number the invariant already has.  That the
token array's own depth agrees with `sc.flowLevel` is a CROSS-CHECK on the
definition rather than a dependency, and it is measured rather than assumed:
`flowTokenDepth = flowLevel` at **every step** of every input of length ≤ 6 over
an eleven-symbol flow alphabet — 1 771 561 inputs, **1 638 834 steps**, maximum
depth 6, no disagreement — and over the repository's own `examples/` (139 files,
1 562 steps).  The alphabet carries both brackets, both closes, the two
separators, a node, a `[96]` property and the three things that END a token
(Reflection 614: adjacency is manufactured by termination).  CI carries the
length-≤ 4 sweep (14 641 inputs, 27 143 steps) as four `#guard`s; the longer
bound is stated here as a measurement with its alphabet, not as a claim about
all inputs.

**The gate, priced by the compiler.**  Guard `FlowBaseRoutes.value` with a
`Prop` and build: **ten** sites, and only one of them is work.

| class | sites | pays with |
|---|---|---|
| `FlowBaseRoutes.ofValue` | 1 | forwards to its own caller |
| the six open arms with a non-park route — doc-suffix ×2, fresh document, bare document, block value, compact entry | 6 | nothing; the gate is ignored |
| **the props arm** (`h_route` — item 160's §3) | **1** | the park's own verdict |
| the two base closes (`resume.value`) | 2 | `danglingNodePos?_flowClose_reads_park` |

So the gate rides the structure as a PARAMETER — the shape `kc` already has
(item 75: "a PARAMETER, not an index … nests forward it untouched and read
nothing from it") — six arms pass `True`, the props arm passes
`danglingNodePos? sc = none`, and the two closes pay it.

**The reading at the close, measured.**  `a: 1⏎&p [b]`: the park's array is
**11** tokens when the `[` arrives, so the open lands at index 11 — `o =
s_park.tokens.size`, the identity `FlowOpenHeld` carries — and at the `]` the
stack read at the close's own index is still `[11]`, with `flowOpenIdx?`
returning `some 11`.  That is what turns the close's verdict into the park's,

`invalidBareDocument 1,0` and `a: 1⏎&p [b]: c` scans clean, which is why the
verdict has to reach the close rather than be decided at the open.

### Item 162 (2026-09-13)

**The park a flow frame was opened over, anchored across its interior — and the
installation priced by the compiler.**  Item 161 read the bracket balance
FORWARD and proved the two readings the same, which is what makes the hold
maintainable one push at a time.  What it did not close is the DISTANCE: the
hold `danglingNodePos?_flowClose_reads_park` needs is a fact about the state at
the CLOSE, and the close is an arbitrary number of steps from the open that
established it.  This item is the carrier that crosses that distance.

**The anchor.**  `ParkAnchor sc0 s d` says three things about `s` and one about
the park `sc0` the frame was opened over: the token array agrees with the
park's BELOW the open; the open is still HELD, `d` nests deep, in
`flowOpenIdxStack`; the indent stack is the park's; and the park itself is out
of flow and ends in a `[96] c-ns-properties` property.  `FlowBaseAnchor` lifts
it over `Option ScannerState` and `GateOf` is the verdict it gates —
`danglingNodePos? sc0 = none` at `some`, `True` at `none` — so a frame whose
enclosing construct owes an unconditional node reading carries `none` and pays
NOTHING.  That is six of the ten `FlowBaseRoutes.value` sites item 161 priced,
free by construction rather than by argument.

**A step can do FIVE things to it, and the fifth is not a push.**  Four were
expected — write no token, write one that is neither bracket, write an open,
write a close.  The fifth was found by asking what the flow interior actually
does to the array: a simple key's resolution REWRITES, turning the two slots
the save reserved into the `[187] c-l-block-map-implicit-key` pair.  Token
equality cannot state that the stack survives it; `flowOpenIdxStack_congr_kind`
can, because the stack reads only `isFlowOpen` and `isFlowClose` and neither
the placeholder nor the `key` that replaces it is a bracket.  `preprocess` and
`adUpdate` are the two silent writers every flow dispatch passes through
before its own push, spelled once here rather than at each arm; `gate` is what
the base close spends.

**The anchor, measured.**  The park in `a: 1⏎&p [b, [c]]` is **11** tokens when
the `[` arrives, so the base open lands at index 11 and the nest at 18, and the
whole interior is one table:

```
sz=11 fl=0 stk=[]       ; sz=12 fl=1 stk=[11]     ; sz=15 fl=1 stk=[11]
sz=16 fl=1 stk=[11]     ; sz=19 fl=2 stk=[18, 11] ; sz=22 fl=2 stk=[18, 11]
sz=23 fl=1 stk=[11]     ; sz=24 fl=0 stk=[]
```

The prefix below 11 is unchanged at every one of those steps, and the stack's
LENGTH is the scanner's own `flowLevel` throughout — item 161's cross-check,
now read on a nested frame.

**What the close can and cannot decide.**  §9.2's verdict is `some 1,0` at the
park, `none` right through the interior (a flow is exempt), and `some 1,0`
again at the depth-0 close — and that last reading is **the same for the input
the scanner refuses and the input it accepts**.  `a: 1⏎&p [b]` is
`invalidBareDocument 1,0`; `a: 1⏎&p [b]: c` scans clean; both read `dangling`
at the `]` and differ only at the `:` one step LATER.  So the gate cannot be
settled at the open — the park is dangling there either way — and it is not
settled by the close's position either.  The close hands the verdict to the
park it makes, and that park's own face (`pendingContent`'s `h_closable`, item
157) is what finally pays it.  That is why `FlowBaseAnchor.gate` takes
`danglingNodePos? s_cl = none` as a HYPOTHESIS rather than proving it.

**The installation, priced by the compiler.**  The tower was given the gate

| what pays | count | how it pays |
|---|---|---|
| signatures ascribing `FlowBaseRoutes`/`FlowOpenStack`/`FlowStackB` | **46** | one `{g : Option ScannerState}` binder each; every constructor application and every `cases` compiles verbatim |
| `FlowStackK` constructions at depth **0** | ~50 | **nothing** — the conjunct sits under `0 < fl`, which they already discharge by `absurd` |
| `FlowStackK` constructions at POSITIVE depth | **~20** | one of the five shapes above, per arm |
| `FlowBaseRoutes.value` | **10** | item 161's table |

sk=true/1 [S,ph,ph,&]            sk=false/0 [S,ph,ph,&,[]
sk=true/5 [S,ph,ph,&,[,ph,ph,s]  sk=false/0 [S,ph,ph,&,[,ph,K,s,V]

rather than asserted.

### Item 164 (2026-09-14)

**The reservation floor — and the gate it lets the close pay.**  Item 163
measured the obstacle and left the anchor conjunct out of the invariant.  This
item carries the precondition it named, lands the conjunct with all twenty
arms, and spends the gate at the two base closes, which is what makes the
carrier load-bearing rather than merely built.

**One predicate, two readings.**  `KeyFloor ts o k` says an ARMED simple key's
reservation sits above `o`, is in bounds, and holds no bracket.  Those are
exactly the two things item 162's fifth shape needs.  `scanValuePrepare` in
flow writes ONE slot — `simpleKey.tokenIndex + 1` — so the park's prefix
survives the write iff that slot is above the base open, and the forward
bracket stack survives it iff the slot's KIND does not change, which it does
not: `[193]`'s `key` is no more a bracket than the placeholder it replaces.  An
unarmed key promises nothing, and that is what makes every clearing step free —
`:`, `?`, `,`, the block scalars and both opens all discharge their half by
construction.

**The range is DEPTH-RELATIVE, and `Nat` makes it free.**  `ParkFloor sc0 s d`
carries the floor for the pending key and for the top `d` entries of
`simpleKeyStack`.  It cannot carry it for all of them: a flow close RESTORES
the pending key from that stack, and the base close restores the key that was
pending OUTSIDE the flow — in `&p [a: b]` a reservation at index 1 against an
open at 4.  That is sound because a closed frame owes no anchor, so what the
floor covers is everything ABOVE the base slot.  The arithmetic then costs
nothing: an open takes `(size, d)` to `(size + 1, d + 1)`, a close takes
`(size, d + 1)` to `(size - 1, d)`, and `size - d` is invariant under both,
with truncating subtraction agreeing at every degenerate case.  The new range
at an open is the old range plus the key just stacked, and at a close a
sub-range of the old — so neither transport needs a size side condition.

**Every obligation is inside a WRAPPER, which is why the arms are a replay.**
Five shapes maintain the floor and each is stated against the scanner's own
function: the SAVE (preprocessing, the only step that opens a reservation — and
it pays from the anchor itself, since a held open is an index INTO the array
the save extends), the two OPENS (stack the pending key, clear it), the two
CLOSES (pop it back), and the `:` (rewrite and clear).  Three step-shape
lemmas were needed under them, all read off functions that already existed:
`preprocess_floor_cases` — which takes the array shape and the key shape out of
ONE `split`, because a fresh index with an untouched array would leave the
reserved slot out of bounds and nothing rules that out when the two shapes come
from two separate lemmas — `scanValue_inFlow_tokens_shape`, and
`dispatchContent_pending_cases`, the whole content lane in one reading (a
content dispatch keeps the reservation where it was — the quoted scalars move
only `endLine` — or clears it; none OPENS one).

**The conjunct, landed with all twenty arms.**  `FlowStackK` carries
`FlowBaseAnchor g sc (fl - 1)` under `0 < fl`.  The arms are **exactly twenty**,
and they split as item 163's measurement said they would: fifteen were already
mechanical (the two opens, the two nested closes, four `,`, the `?`, and the six
content arms), and the remaining **five** are the `:` — one in each of
`accum_step_block`'s `.value`, `.colon` and `.question` gap cases — which
`FlowBaseAnchor.flowValue` now closes.  Each step lemma names the anchor twice
and nowhere else: once off the invariant (`h_panch`), once across the two silent
writers every dispatch crosses (`h_panch_ad`).

**And the gate, PAID.**  `FlowBaseRoutes.value` takes `GateOf g`.  Item 161
priced that at **ten** sites and the landed cost is exactly its table: `ofValue`
forwards, the six open arms with an unconditional route ignore the premise

two base closes spend `FlowBaseAnchor.gate_of_close` — the anchor's four
readings are the bracket push's own, and the only thing the arm supplies is
§9.2's verdict on the state it just made, which is precisely the premise
`pendingContent.h_closable` already hands it.  The one site still choosing
`none` where it could choose `some` is the props arm, which is the tenth.

**Witnessed in `Tests/Guards/Proofs/FlowReservationFloor.lean`**, where §5

### Item 165 (2026-09-14)

**`[96]`'s LENGTH — and the gate, the guard and the residue it pays for.**  Item
164 named what was left in two and put them in that order: the props arm, then
`pendingProps.h_route` taking §9.2's verdict.  Building the SECOND first is what
showed the order was wrong, and what the obstacle was.

**The guard does not relay through a run's own EXTENSION, and item 160 priced
that class as free.**  `trailingNodeRun?` walks back over at most TWO
properties, because `[96] c-ns-properties` derives at most one anchor and one
tag.  A third property therefore MOVES §9.2's start — from the run's first
property to its second — so the park's reading and the reading one push later
are readings of different tokens.  `PropsRunReadingTransport` §1 measured that
move when item 160 built the relay, and its own prose said so; the table beside
it counted the extension among the eleven rides the relay pays.  Only one of the
two is right, and the table was the wrong one.

**What unblocks it is the SCANNER, not the proof.**  Both §6.9 guards decide by
KIND, and outside a flow they read `trailingPropertyRunOnLine` — the current
LINE's run.  That reading is blind to a run crossing a break: at the `&b` of
`&a⏎!t &b x` the line's run is `[!t]`, which carries no anchor, so the third
property was accepted and only `TokenParser` refused the document.
`propertyRunFull` decides by LENGTH and reads the RUN, so where the run's breaks
fall no longer changes the answer — and with the third property refused, the
walk-back never reaches its cap at a park the scanner produces.  ~~Every input it
refuses is already `[96]`-invalid: two anchors or two tags on one node.~~  It
costs ONE definition on each pipeline and one disjunct on each of the four
property guards, and it fires on **nothing**: 0 of 847 `.yaml` files (the repo's
143 and the suite's 704), with `eventscore`, `suiterunner` and the 4497-check
suite unmoved.

> **Refuted by item 169's matrix re-run.**  A FULL run for a parent node
> followed across the break by a fresh run for its block mapping's first
> implicit key is `[96]`-valid twice over, and the gate reads the two runs as
> one: **9KAX** (`&a4 !!map⏎&a5 !!str key5: value4`) now rejects on both
> pipelines — matrix 402/402 → 401/402, JSON 282/282 → 281/282.  The census
> above did not contain the refuting input: it scanned the suite's `src` form
> (the META files), and the input exists in the matrix checkout's data form.
> Probe-verified: at the refusal state only the `propertyRunFull` disjunct
> fires.  The correction is item 169's named next item — **fixed at item 170**:
> in block context the gate fires only when all three properties share the
> cursor's line, and the matrix stands at 402/402 + 282/282 again.

**Then the guard lands, and the table pays as item 160 wrote it.**
`pendingProps.h_route` takes `danglingNodePos? sc = none`, and building names

### Item 166 (2026-09-14)

**The block landing's surviving branch — and the family seven forecasts did not
name.**  Item 139 halved `bareNodeRoute`'s domain at the block landing and left
the other half whole, and every item since has forecast that half the same way:
"its `-` family the scanner already refuses, its `:`/`?` family is LEGAL and
routes through the key cascade, so what is left is a CONSUMER to narrow."  The
conclusion is right.  The reason is not, and the `-` half of it is false.

**What refuses `a: 1⏎- x` is not the open level.**  `scanBlockEntryValidate`
conjoins THREE readings — the stack's top is a mapping at this column, no node
slot is awaited, and no same-indent sequence is open — and refuses only when all
three hold.  The forecast read the first conjunct as the whole test.  Lift the
third and the identical landing is legal:

```
- a:            - - a          a:             k:
    b: 1        - b            - x              a:
- c                            - y              - x
                                                - y
```

all four scan clean, parse clean, arrive at this branch behind a COMPLETED node
with a level open at the landing's own column, and are the next entry of a
`[183] l+block-sequence` that is already open there.  §8.2.1's auto-detected `m`
is allowed to be 0, so a sequence at its parent mapping's own column is never
pushed onto the indent stack and is visible in the TOKEN ARRAY alone — which is
why the two readings sit in two different places and why no stack test can find
the second one.

**The branch is therefore not refutable, and this item proves it rather than
asserting it.**  `blockEntry_landing_openSeq` derives `OpenSeqEntry` from the
DISPATCH itself: a park with a completed tail awaits no node
(`nodeSlotAwaited_false_of_landing`, `DanglingPred` read through
`slotHolderIdx?` and carried across preprocessing by item 157's transport), so a
`-` that scanned at all did so with a sequence open at this column.  Over the
490-file corpus the branch is taken **134** times in **54** files, every one of
them with `sameIndentSequenceOpen` true and **none** outside the theorem.

**So what row 1c needs here is a ROUTE, not a guard**, and the route is named:
`∀ sp_e, SBlockSeqEntries k sp_mid sp_e → SLYamlStream sp_start sp_e` for a
collection already open at the landing's width.  No park carries one at that
width.  `pendingBlockContent.h_closable_entry` is exactly that shape at the
park's OWN width `n`, and `accum_block_on_pendingBlockContent` spends it for the
sibling `-` under its own `by_cases hkn : k = n` — so what is left for this
branch is that lemma's `k ≠ n` arm and the `pendingContent` park, which has no
entry-level route of any width.  Item
155's `ResumeFrames` record MAPPING levels by construction — the `-` opens a
sequence level, so the cover crosses the step untouched and the list is the
mapping widths alone — so ~~the sequence's own resume twin is the item behind
this one~~.

### Item 167 (2026-09-14)

**The sequence lane's dedent — and the half of item 166's residue the corpus

item builds it.  Measuring the domain first — item 166's own lesson — split it

**What the unwind drops decides which half.**  A dedenting `-` closes every
level above its column and continues the collection AT it, so what the landing
needs is one width and not a stack of them.  Over the 490-file corpus
the scanner dispatches **530** block entries; **76** land after an unwind that
dropped a level; and in **all 76** every dropped level is a block MAPPING.
**`dropSeq = 0`** — not one `-` in 490 files dedents out of an open block
SEQUENCE, and no file contains such a shape at all.  Re-reading item 166's own
134 surviving-branch landings on the PARK's state rather than the post-unwind
one says the same thing from the other side: **58** land at the park's own top
level (the sibling `pendingBlockContent`'s `k = n` arm serves), **76** land
strictly below it, and `popSq = 0`.

**The absent half is legal, and the parser already reads it the way this item
routes it.**  `- - a⏎- b` scans, parses, and emits

collection's second ENTRY, not a second bare document — and `-⏎␣␣-⏎- b` and
`- - - a⏎- b` likewise.  No file among the 490 contains one, so §1 of the
guard file has to write the shape out to show it at all.

**`SeqEntryTail` is the lane's bottom**, and the `ExplValueLine` of it (item
108's parameter, read on the sequence side): `SeqEntryTail sp_start ke sp_e` is
the enclosing `[183]`'s `[186]` tail, still owed at `sp_e`.  Closing it at

spends it instead, consing the landing's own entry onto what is left.  It is the

**Two park fields, one payer, two spends.**  `pendingBlock.h_seqF` and

### Item 168 (2026-09-14)

**The compact mapping that fills a sequence entry — and the 76 the corpus
actually has.**  Item 167 built `SeqEntryTail`, paid it on the two ENTRY parks,
and measured that the corpus puts nothing there: over 490 files not one
dedenting `-` crosses an open block SEQUENCE.  This item takes the same
predicate to the park the corpus's dedenting `-` does stand on.

**Where they park, measured before anything was built.**  Re-reading item 166's
134 surviving-branch landings: of the **76** whose unwind drops a level, the
token BEFORE the park's tail is a `:` in **75** of them.  The park is a mapping
VALUE's content — `pendingContent` — which neither of item 167's fields reaches,
so the collection's tail can only arrive there by crossing the `:` with the key
and coming back out with the value.  `atSeq = 74` land back on a sequence level
the indent stack holds; **2** land where §8.2.1's auto-detected `m` is 0 and the
sequence sits at its parent mapping's own column, so the level at `k` reads `M`
and the collection is in the TOKEN ARRAY alone
([example-2.27](examples/2/example-2.27.yaml),
[example-2.28](examples/2/example-2.28.yaml)).  The route is indifferent to that
split: `SeqEntryTail` is a production, not a stack entry.

**And how far it has to travel, measured second.**  The same 76 by drop depth:
`drop1 = 68`, all of them MAPPING levels, `drop2 = 8`, `drop3p = 0`.  So ONE
open level covers 68 and nothing in the corpus wants three — item 167's choice
of one width, made again, for the same reason and against a second measurement.
Then the 68 by whether the entry they dedent OUT of spans one line:
**`oneLine = 6`, `multiLine = 62`**.  That number decided the item's shape: the
compact `:` alone buys six, and what buys the rest is the face surviving a
SIBLING key landing — a hop that closes nothing and must therefore CONS.

**The cascade's head is free.**  `pendingBlockContent.h_closable_entry` is
`∀ sp_mid, SSLComments sp_scan sp_mid → ∀ sp_end, SCompactSeqTail n sp_mid sp_end
→ SLYamlStream sp_start sp_end`, which is `SeqEntryTail sp_start n` at the park's
own width, definitionally — and `pendingBlock.h_close_entry` is its node-shaped
twin.  Both are UNCONDITIONAL fields, so every producer already pays them and the
chain starts with an identity rather than a new obligation.

**What the field is.**  One width, tail riding, everything below fused:

* `ImplicitKeyPack` gains a fourth twin beside items 93, 99 and 108 — the same
  entry and the same `SCompactMapTail`, ending at the enclosing `[183]`'s
  remaining tail instead of the finished stream.
* `pendingMapValue.h_seqF` is `h_close`'s sequence twin at the park's own level;
  `pendingContent.h_seqF` is the same with `SSLComments` in the node's place and

* `ResumeKeyCtx` gains the landing's own reading of it, and the test this lane
  runs is EQUALITY, not membership: the face names one level, so the landing
  either stands at that width or the collection is out of reach.

**What pays and what punts.**  `entryKeyPack_of_dispatch`'s COMPACT branch pays
from the caller's entry closure — the key on the indicator's own line wraps into

node, not to one that fills the entry.  `content_dispatch_routed`'s RESUMING

`accum_content_on_pendingMapValue_indented` pays all three of its content parks;
the ROOT arm has no such parameter at all, because a `pendingMapValue` at index 0

**Price: TWO new declarations, no runtime change** — `seqEntryTail_mapCons` and
`pendingContent`/`pendingMapValue`'s fields, plus one conjunct each on

**A green build is not evidence here, and the record should say so.**  Every

### Item 169 (2026-09-15)

**One move pays all nine.**  The face becomes

**What pays and what punts.**  `entryKeyPack_of_dispatch` gains `h_nodeSF` —

crossed-window arms' scanner-reachable domain is EMPTY.**  The M4 candidate
the census named at item 174, landed not as a new check but as a widening of
`danglingNodePos?` (and its indexed twin): the readers gain a fourth clause,
`crossedPropsExcessPos?`, checked AFTER the at-level reading so every position
they reported before this item is unchanged.

**The reading.**  `[96] c-ns-properties` admits one anchor and one tag, so an
ADJACENT block of property tokens holding two of one kind is never one run.
It can still be TWO runs — `[200]`'s collection properties, a break, then the
first KEY's own run — but that split resolves on the KEY's OWN LINE (a
block-key context admits no break), so at a line end the discrimination is
over: a trailing run whose adjacent block duplicates a kind has no derivation,
whatever follows.  `propsBlockScanLoop` walks the block UNCAPPED (the
`trailingPropertyRun` cap is the legal run's arity, and this reader exists to
see past it), and the excess — the first token, in token order, whose kind
repeats — is the position `TokenParser.validNextToken` reports for these
inputs, so the twelve parser-refused shapes in the item's battery move stage
with the constructor AND position byte-identical (`&a⏎!t &b x` at `1,3`,
`&a !t⏎&b x` at `1,0`, `!t⏎&a !u x`, `&a⏎!t⏎&b x`, `&a⏎!t &b⏎x: 1`,
`---`/`...`/depth/`- ` variants, the no-body `&a⏎!t &b` at EOF).  The
same-line thirds never get this far — the push guards refuse them at the
character — so the clause catches exactly the families whose internal
separation CROSSED a break: `PropsWindowCross`, read by the runtime.

**Measured before building, against PyYAML (6.x, `yaml.parse`).**  A
33-input battery: the SPLIT family is accepted by both with identical
readings (`&a⏎!t &b x: 1` = `+MAP &a` with the key decorated `!t &b`,
`&a⏎&k k: 1`, `!t⏎&a !u x: 1`, `&outer⏎&inner b: 1` — the healing that
makes a push-time refusal UNSOUND and fixes the check point at the break);
the one-run internal-break family is untouched (`!t⏎&q b`, `!t⏎&q⏎b` — one
decorated scalar, both parsers); and every input the clause refuses, PyYAML
refuses.  THREE readings move beyond stage:

### Item 181 (2026-09-16)

**The crossed-window arms, RETIRED** — item 180's proof half, and the first
item in this row whose whole content is a DELETION.  Item 180 moved the
crossed over-full property block's refusal into the scanner; this one spends
the shrinkage: `PropsWindowCross`, `propsWindowCross_push_refute` and
`pendingProps.h_routeX` are gone, with the six payments the field cost, and
`content_dispatch_routed`'s route premise is `ContentRouteGate` alone again.
ZERO runtime code: the one runtime edit is a docstring sentence in
`TokenQueries.lean` that named a now-deleted declaration.

**The pigeonhole.**  `[96] c-ns-properties` admits one anchor and one tag, so
THREE adjacent property tokens always duplicate a kind.  A property push onto
a crossed window makes exactly three — the window's below-token, the park's
tail, and the pushed one — so §9.2's fourth clause reads an excess and
`danglingNodePos?` returns `some`.  Measured first
(`Scratch/Probe181.lean`): all EIGHT kind assignments report an excess, with
and without placeholder gaps, and the two-property controls stay `none`
exactly when the kinds differ; then pinned exhaustively in the guard
(`PropsCrossWindowRoute` §2, 12 new `#guard`s).

**The shape is the point.**  Item 170 read the slide correctly — §9.2's
walk-back is capped at `[96]`'s arity, so the window moves under a property
push and the two verdicts are readings of different columns — and concluded
that `propsPark_dangling_of_prop`'s conclusion was FALSE at a
scanner-reachable state, so no strengthening of premises could fix it.  That
was true when written.  What it did not ask is whether the state stays
reachable: items 178 and 180 refused both halves of the window's domain at
the scanner, and with the domain empty the relay holds *vacuously* —
its own premise is what fails in the branch that could not transport.  A
transport lemma that cannot be proved is a question about its SOURCE states,
not only about the target; the bypass is worth building only after the
reachability is measured.  Item 170's bypass was not wasted (the family
scanned clean then), but its retirement is what the two runtime items were
for.

**The kit** (six lemmas, `StreamAccum`): `not_placeholder_of_isNodeProperty`
and `isAnchor_or_isTag_of_isNodeProperty` (the two holes);
`propsBlockScanLoop_two_props` — past a property and the property below it
the scan has an excess OR both flags, which is the half that does not depend
on what comes next; `propsBlockScanLoop_excess_of_saturated` — a third
closes it; `crossedPropsExcessPos?_push_prop_three` — the two composed at the
pushed array, reusing `_push_prop_mono`'s own reduction;
`danglingNodePos?_ne_none_of_crossed` — a run that STARTS on a property
clears the slot exemption, so BOTH remaining branches report and an excess is
a verdict at whatever column.

**What the deletion takes with it.**  `propsPark_dangling_of_prop` loses its
disjunct AND two premises — `propertyRunFull s_ad = false` and the tail's
`pos.line = sc.line` conjunct, both of which existed only to establish the
window's line disagreement — so it is now premise-for-premise
`propsPark_dangling_of_body`'s twin.  Two residues, recorded rather than
chased: `propertyRunFull_false_of_anchor_dispatch`/`_tag_dispatch` have no
production consumer left (pinned in `PropsRunLengthGate` §1 and
`PropsRunReadingTransport`), and `propsPark_prevReal_prop`'s line conjunct is
now weakened away at both of its call sites (pinned in `PropsRunLengthGate`
§3).  Neither is vestigial by the produce-cost test: both are read off runs
the callers already hold.

**What it buys the flip.**  `accum_content_pending`'s two raw `bareNodeRoute`
applications — the crossed arms — are gone, so the raw-route census drops
from **THREE** holders to **TWO** (`bareNodeRoute_or_refused_content` ×2,
`content_dispatch_after_close` ×1, both at their item-176 counts).  At the

### Item 182 (2026-09-16)

**The `k: &x⏎a` runtime floor** — the flip's last prerequisite of any kind,
and §9.2's FIFTH dangling reading.  Items 177 and 178 read Finding A in
FRONT of the trailing run: a scalar, alias or `[96]`-headed run standing at an
open level's own column has no derivation, because every alternative of
`[196] s-l+block-node(n,c)` and `[185] s-l+block-indented(n,c)` it can head
spends `s-separate(n+1)`.  The same separator sits INSIDE the run, between
`[96]`'s properties and the content they decorate, and a run may start LEGALLY
and cross the break there: in `k: &x⏎a` the `&x` is at column 3, where no
level stands, and it is the CONTENT that lands at the mapping's own column 0.
The run-start reading cannot see it; this one reads the token that starts the
run's next line, which is where the crossed `s-separate(n+1)` is spent.

**The reading is `crossedPropsExcessIdx?`'s own three arms** (item 180's),
and that is the whole design.  `propsBlockLineCrossLoop` scans DOWN the
adjacent property block and reports the first property, in token order, whose
real predecessor is a property on an EARLIER line — `[96]`'s internal
separation spent across a break — and `runLineCrossPos?` dispatches it exactly
as the crossed reading does: a property tail, a one-token body (with the
props→body crossing as its second reading), a flow close read back to its own
open.  Reading the block AT THE CLOSE is what keeps a park's verdict and its
collection's the same one, which is why `danglingNodePos?_flowClose_reads_park`
survives as an EQUALITY rather than needing a premise the reachable states
happen to satisfy.  The first design read the run's tokens positionally from
the run's start and skipped the flow arm; it left `k: &a⏎!t [1]` accepted
(PyYAML refuses it) and made that lemma false.  **A clause that mirrors an
existing clause's dispatch inherits its kit and its transports; one that
invents its own inherits neither.**

**Measured before any Lean was written.**  PyYAML 6.0.3 at `yaml.parse` on 47
inputs: it refuses every family member at the CONTENT's own position — which
is the position `runLineCrossPos?` reports — and accepts every control (the
same-line props `k: &x a`, the strictly deeper landing `k: &x⏎ a` at every
depth, the sibling key `k: &x⏎b: 2`, the seq-spaces entry `k: &x⏎- a`, the
sibling flow key `k: &a⏎!t [1]: b`, and the ROOT and marker runs `&x⏎a`,
`---⏎&x⏎a`, where no level stands at the content's column).  The ONE
disagreement is the block-scalar form `k: &x⏎|⏎␣x`, which PyYAML accepts
against `[199]`'s own `s-separate(n+1)` — **item 177's named PyYAML gap, read
one step over**, and refusing it here is what our own `k:⏎|⏎␣x` already does.
`: &x⏎a` is refused by both, at different positions: PyYAML trips on the
leading `:` at `0,0`, we report the crossing at `1,0`.

**The corpus census ran BEFORE the runtime was touched**, as an
over-approximation: the candidate clause evaluated at EVERY state the scan
visits (which is every `s_run` either check can read), ignoring the
`simpleKeyAllowed` gate, so an entry it does not name cannot change.  Over the
402 `in.yaml` leaves it named **TWO**:

* **H7J7** (`node-anchor-not-indented`, `key: &x⏎!!map⏎␣␣a: b`) — an ERROR
  case, refused by the parser's `trailingContent` at `1,0` and now by the
  scanner at `1,0`.  The stage moves, the position does not, and PyYAML
  reports the same `1,0`.  The suite decides this reading, which is better
  evidence than PyYAML alone.
* **6KGN** (`---⏎a: &anchor⏎b: *anchor`) — a VALID case, and a false positive
  of the census's own over-approximation: the clause fires at the state after
  `b` is scanned and before its `:`, and no gated check reads that state.  It
  is the mechanism that keeps `a: 1⏎b: 2` alive — at that same state
  `danglingNodePos?` has ALWAYS returned `some` — and 6KGN is untouched.

One more moved, outside the suite: the mutation row **`6KGN:0 b:*anchor no
space`** (`---⏎a: &anchor⏎b:*anchor`).  Without the space `b:*anchor` is one
plain scalar rather than a key, so it is the `&anchor` run's own content
landing at the mapping's column.  libyaml rejected it and we accepted it; the
row moves from `LENIENT: libyaml rejects` to `BOTH_REJECT`, and PyYAML agrees
at the same `2,0`.  **A leniency closing is a suite edit, and the edit is the
finding** — the row's own label was the record of the divergence.

**The proof cost is the transports, and one of them is now an implication.**
`danglingNodePos?_congr` takes a SIXTH premise (`runLineCrossPos?` equal on
the two arrays) and `danglingNodePos?_none_mono` a disjunctive one (the
target's reading is `none`, or it is the source's), and the two pushes pay it
from the block reading alone: a body or property pushed onto a `[96]` park
leaves the block below it untouched across the reservation gap, so the park's
crossing is the pushed state's FIRST reading and the push's own is the second.
`danglingNodePos?_dispatch_body_onProp` therefore **weakens from an equality
to the `none` direction** — the content a park takes may be the token that
starts a line, so the push can be refused where the park was clean, which is
`k: &x⏎a` itself.  Every consumer wanted only that direction
(`propsPark_dangling_of_body`, and the guard example that pinned it), which is
item 181's lesson read forward: **when a runtime floor refuses more, ask which
direction of each transport the consumers actually spend before repairing the
equality.**

**Two findings recorded, neither this item's.**

* **A legacy/indexed divergence on undefined aliases at a dangling position.**
  `a: 1⏎*p` (and `k:⏎*p`, `k: &x⏎*p`) refuses as `undefinedAlias "p" 1 0` in
  the legacy pipeline and `invalidBareDocument 1 0` in the indexed one — the
  two order the alias check and §9.2's EOF check differently.  Both refuse, at
  the same position, so the matrix (which scores error tests on "errors at
  all") has never seen it and does not now; `k: *p` agrees exactly, which is
  what says the divergence is the ORDER and not the check.  Found by this
  item's probe, predates it, and is not in its scope.
* **The `[210]` flip's surface did not move.**  The instrument still reports
  FIVE errors at the same five definitions AND the same five lines —
  `topLevelFlowResumeSep` 4190, `rootMapRoute` 5470, `rootMapRouteF` 5493,
  `bareNodeRoute` 5662, `structural_dispatch_to_pending` 7114 — because this
  item's kit lands below all five.  That is the expected reading: the five are
  the flip's WORK (the four raw routes plus the wrapper it deletes), never its
  blockers; what a prerequisite buys is that no accepted input still needs the
  bare arm.

**No refusal is weakened and none is added beyond the reading.**  The clause
is checked LAST — after the slot exemption, the at-level reading and the
crossed block — so every position `danglingNodePos?` reported before item 182
is unchanged, and `k: &x⏎[1]`/`k: &a !t⏎[1]` keep item 172's
`underIndentedFlowContent 1 0` because the flow INTERIOR is that reading's,

explicit-value ride, whose own input is the family (props at column 2, content
at 0); it is refused at `2,0` and PyYAML refuses it there too, with the deeper
`? k⏎: &p⏎␣b` pinned beside it as the ride the arm still serves.

### Item 183 (2026-09-16)

**The `[210]` flip, PRICED by its domain — and the price left as an instrument
rather than a number.**

Row 19's closing sentence has read, since item 182, that the narrowing's
prerequisite list is EMPTY.  It is, of RUNTIME floors: every input that used to
need a raw route for a reading the scanner has since refused is out of the
domain (items 177–182).  What it does not say is that the flip is one session's
work, and §9's rule for an escape hatch is to enumerate the input classes that
still exit through it, by measurement, before writing any number.  This item
does that, and leaves two gates behind so the measurement is re-derivable
instead of remembered.

**The flip instrument is not the instrument this needs.**  Flipping
`SLYamlStream.implicitContinue`'s `[210]` slot to `GOpt SLExplicitDocument`
reports FIVE errors — re-measured here at `topLevelFlowResumeSep` 4190,
`rootMapRoute` 5470, `rootMapRouteF` 5493, `bareNodeRoute` 5662,
`structural_dispatch_to_pending` 7114, unchanged in position since item 180's
re-count and in COUNT since item 166.  It cannot move before the flip lands,
because the five ARE the flip: the four raw routes it deletes and the one
`SLAnyDocument.explicit` wrapper it unwraps.  Item after item has quoted that
five as a standing instrument, which it is — of the WORK, never of the
remainder.  **The number that measures the remainder is the one below, and it
did not exist until this item.**

**The surface a payment does move, pinned.**
[`Tests/Guards/Proofs/FlipConsumerSurface.lean`](Tests/Guards/Proofs/FlipConsumerSurface.lean)
counts, from the elaborated environment, every `StreamAccum` constant that
applies one of the four raw routes or one of the five guards standing in front
of them: **EIGHT definitions, FIFTEEN applications** — one raw
(`content_dispatch_after_close: bareNodeRoute=1`) and seven guard holders
carrying the other fourteen.  `Scratch/CensusRawRoutes.lean` could not see this:
it skips the guards, which is what makes it say each raw term is written once
(TWO holders, since item 181), and every payment row 19 has left removes a
GUARD application rather than a raw one.  The denominator is named on the file:
`StreamAccum`'s own module, because other guard files apply the routes in worked
examples that document their interfaces, and the module filter is what keeps

### Item 185 (2026-09-17)

**Class A's NINE are three questions with three prices — and the split that
named them was two thirds of a total one.**

Item 184 put U2's residue first and priced it at nine applications.  §9's rule
applies to a class exactly as it applies to an escape: enumerate what still
exits, by measurement, before writing a number.  Doing that to the nine found
three different missing things, and found the branch that reaches them stated
more weakly than the reading it was named for.

**The discriminator was incomplete, and that is why the branch had nothing to
spend.**  `scanValue` computes

    explicitValue = s_kc.explicitKeyLine.isSome && !s_kc.simpleKey.possible
                      && (s.inFlow || (s.col : Int) == s_kc.explicitKeyCol)

with `s_kc = scanValueClearKey s`.  Item 125's split reads the FIRST and the
THIRD conjunct.  The middle one — the saved key that SURVIVES the clear — is a
field of the same state, decidable there like the other two, and leaving it out
did not make the escape's branch smaller: it made it UNNAMED.  The negation of
a two-alternative disjunction is strictly weaker than `explicitValue = true`,
so the branch could not be spent even where every input in it satisfies the
stronger statement.  `scanValue_stamp_of_cleared_key` supplies the third
alternative (`scanValue_stamp_of_key`'s proof with its premise taken where the
definition takes it, so it needs one hypothesis rather than three), and
`scanValue_stamp_of_src` now joins all three.

**What the third alternative is WORTH, measured before it was spent.**  At the
runtime it removes NOTHING: over 5 186 accepted three-line programs, the number
carrying a class-A landed `:` is **1 412 under item 125's split and 1 412 under
the widened one**.  So this is not a domain narrowing and is not recorded as
one.  What it buys is that the negation is now exactly `explicitValue = true` —
the `:` IS `[197] l-block-map-explicit-value`'s own — and THAT is spendable:
the scanner admitted the dispatch, so §8.2.2 [197]'s own two tests already
passed, and `explicit_at_indent_of_dispatch` reads them back off the same
state — the `:` stands off the `?`'s line and at `s-indent(n)`,
`(col : Int) = currentIndent`.  All nine sites now PRODUCE that equation, so
the datum a route into the `?` frame's value slot has to land on is known
present at every one of them rather than at the ones a reading happened to
check.

**The nine, partitioned in the code: 3 / 4 / 2.**  Each landed-`:` consumer
splits again on the park's value pack (`h_vpack`/`h_kslot`), and that
`by_cases` has exactly two stuck arms; the two consumers with a compact-fill
arm have a third.  Three wrappers replace one, each carrying its branch's own
evidence:

| wrapper | applications | holders | what empties it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_stamp_offcol` | **3** | `closeThenBlock`, `pendingBlock`, `pendingBlockContent` | a reason `nv = k` — the park's pack index and the landing's column |
| `_stamp_nopack` | **4** (→ **3** at item 186: `noPending`'s site was refutable) | the same three, plus `noPending` | a CARRIER — the `?` frame's value slot at the landing's column |
| `_stamp_compact` | **2** | `closeThenBlock`, `pendingBlock` | the stamp itself, or a refutation |

`FlipConsumerSurface`'s DEFERRAL lane counts five names now and was re-pinned
with the rows PREDICTED from the split before the build; it went green on the
first run, which is what says the 3/4/2 was derived rather than read off the
result.

**The classes OVERLAP; only the sites are partitioned.**  `_stamp_compact`'s
two sites hold `inline_residue_of_landing`'s conclusion as well, and the
wrapper takes BOTH premises, so the elaborator certifies the overlap.  Item
184's three "classes" are three branches of the proof, not three disjoint sets
of inputs, and a wrapper's number is a count of SITES.  Its record is corrected
in place above.

**The three routes want three different things, and they price differently.**

* **`_stamp_offcol` (3) is a COUPLING, not a carrier.**  The park HAS the
  value pack; `colon_open_map_explicit` fires only at `nv = k` because
  `[187]`'s `s-indent(n)` is exact.  What is missing is a reason the pack's
  index and the landing's column agree.  The scanner now hands
  `col = currentIndent` at every site, so the shape of the payment is a
  scanner↔surface fact about the pack's index and the indent stack — U3's
  lane, not U2's, and the producers it touches are the ones that PAY the
  pack rather than the ones that read it.
* **`_stamp_nopack` (4) is the class with NOTHING to carry.**  The field's
  other alternative is `True`, so the branch has no proposition to hand a
  wrapper and no discriminator an elaborator can check — the census row is its
  only instrument, which is the same signature R646 reads on a possible
  phantom, here for a different reason.  ~~`accum_block_on_noPending`'s site is
  in it by construction: a virgin park holds no pack.~~  **Corrected at item
  186**: that site was not in the class at all.  The sentence is true and beside
  the point — the site was there because item 125's case split ran at a park
  that can DECIDE the stamp source, and `noPending.h_noek` now does.  Three
  sites remain.  This is U2's residue proper and its price is a CARRIER on the
  park.
* **`_stamp_compact` (2) cannot be paid with a face at all.**  `[189]
  c-l-block-map-implicit-value`'s value is `s-l+block-node`, which has no
  compact alternative and opens no `[188]` entry of its own, so
  `compact_open_map`'s `:` branch needs the stamp and the `?` branch's face
  cannot stand in for it (the file has said so since item 101).  So this class
  empties by REFUTATION or not at all — and the runtime says it is empty.

**The compact route is EMPTY at every input two instruments could build.**
Only a `:` reaches those two sites — the consumers' `hcv.elim` discharges the
`?` arm by `absurd` and the `-` is handled before the split — so the shape is a
MID-LINE `:` standing at a live `explicitKeyCol`.  A sweep of **35 937**
three-line programs over a 33-fragment line alphabet accepts 5 186, of which
1 412 carry a landed class-A `:` and **zero** carry a compact one; all **351**
