## §1 The question a sweep of acceptance cannot answer

β.5's second deletion is `SLYamlStream.scannerDrop`, and the arm that rides it
is the RUN-END half of the flow open's under-run:

    rcases h_ur with ⟨j, sx, hj, h_ind, _h_ws2, h_end | h_tab⟩
    · exact drop_ride                              -- the subject
    · exact (flowOpen_underRunTab_refuted …).elim  -- already refuted

"No accepted scan lands the open below the floor" says the input dies.  What
the arm needs is narrower: does it die *at the step this lemma is proving*?  So
§5 of `Tests/Guards/Proofs/ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.lean` drives `scanNextToken`
itself over the same grid and, for every landing column strictly below a park's
floor, records whether the flow OPEN is ever dispatched and — when it is — how
many steps later the scan dies and at which gate.

    dispatchSweep == (198, 54, 54, 144, 90, 54)
    distances     == [3, 5]

**198 columns, and they split two ways.**

* **54 never reach the lemma.**  `scanNextToken_preprocess` refuses them while
  unwinding, so `h_preprocess : … = .ok (some (s_prep, c))` is already a
  contradiction and no arm is entered.  The second and third counts are that
  reading taken twice: every non-dispatching column is refused by the one gate
  that runs before the dispatch, and a column refused anywhere else would be
  one the hypothesis does not cover.
* **144 dispatch the open** and die three or five steps later — 90 at §8.1's
  floor, 54 at §9.2's dangling run.  Neither distance is zero, which is the
  finding: **there is no column at which the open's own step refuses.**

And the two gates that do refuse are the two the open's own step also runs.
`accum_flow_open_depth0` already takes both readings — `h_dn :
scanNextToken_checkDanglingNode sc s_prep = .ok ()` and `h_bare :
scanNextToken_checkBareDocument s_prep = .ok ()` — and neither helps, because
they are the right checks at the wrong state: `underIndentedFlowValuePos?`
returns `none` unless the last real token is a flow CLOSE, and at the open the
collection has not opened its first entry.  Carrying more of the open's own
checks cannot reach this branch at any price.

**So the three diagnoses need a fourth reading, not a fourth name.**  §10 prices
FALSE at one experiment — build the input the branch describes and run it — and
that is right about the runtime and silent about the proof.  A FALSE branch
whose refutation is non-local prices like a STARVED one: the experiment is
cheap and settles nothing, and the cost is the CARRIER that walks the refusal
back to the step.  Item 264's diagnosis was correct and its price was the
part that had not been measured.

## §2 What the carrier has to deliver, read off the state that refuses

    deathShape == (144, 144, 144, 144, 144)

At the state where the gate fires, over all 144: the collection has **closed**,
the last real token is its **flow close**, the open's column is **still on the
indent stack**, and **exactly one** of the two readings fires — no overlap, no
remainder.  That last count is `underIndentedFlowValuePos?`'s own docstring
claim ("`danglingNodePos?`'s complement on the SLOT") measured rather than
asserted, and it is what says the split is a partition and not a cover.

So the price is **one carried fact, not two**: *the flow collection closes with
the open's column still on the indent stack.*  Whichever reading then owns the
landing, the scan dies.  The producers that fact must cross are the flow
interior's, and one half of it is already proved — `FlowIndentStable`'s
`preprocess_indents_of_inFlow` is exactly "inside a flow, the indents do not
move".

## §3 The grid ends at the open, and that is a knob

    tailSweep == (198, 0, 54, 144, 144)

The same columns with a sibling line after the open's: nothing accepted that
was not accepted before, the same 54/144 split, and all 144 deaths now at the
MID-STREAM gates rather than the end-of-input ones.  The end of input was not
choosing the answer.

The fifth count exists because the perturbation battery caught the pin without
it: `(198, 0, 54, 144)` is *identical* to the end-of-input reading, so the pin
held whether or not a tail was ever appended — a §9 vacuity in a pin written to
check for §9 vacuity.  Counting the mid-stream deaths is what makes it a second
reading.

## §4 β.5's drop, closed out

`SLYamlStream.scannerDrop` has exactly **two** applications in the library —
`DropDependents.expectedDirect` pins `D=4` and two of those are the guards' own
exhibits:

| site | fate |
| --- | --- |
| `dropClose` (`StreamAccum.lean`) | one consumer, `have drop_ride`, taken by the three live arms — **§1's obligation** |
| `PendingNode.close_with_ssl`'s `\| pendingFlow` arm | goes with the constructor |

The `\| pendingFlow` arm census reads **seven**; item 264's flip breaks **six**.
The seventh is `close_with_ssl`'s, and the flip cannot see it because the arm

## §5 Three comments said the arm was refuted, and the gate they named does not exist

All three live arms carried a sentence asserting this branch is refuted, two

`scripts/gate_vocab.py` is that check for the dispatcher's own vocabulary

`families`, `wrapped` and `self` stand beside the verdict because each is a way

### Item 266 (2026-09-26)

Item 265 priced `accum_flow_open_depth0`'s run-end arm as a CARRIER and named
the fact it has to carry: *the flow collection closes with the open's column
still on the indent stack.*  §10 prices a missing carrier by the producers it
touches, and this item is that census.  It found the transport already built,
the datum already available, and the whole bill in three rings of nine
declarations — and it found a second phantom of item 265's exact kind sitting
in the docstring one production over.

## §1 The transport is already here

`ParkAnchor sc0 s d` (`StreamAccum.lean`) runs a fact from a depth-0 flow OPEN
to its CLOSE.  It is not a sketch: `ParkAnchor.dangling_eq` SPENDS it at the
close, and its premises are item 265's `deathShape` component for component —

    hpre   : ∀ j, j < s_bc.tokens.size → s_cl.tokens[j]! = s_bc.tokens[j]!
    hind   : s_cl.indents = s_bc.indents
    hflow  : s_cl.inFlow = false
    hlast  : prevRealIdx? s_cl.tokens s_cl.tokens.size = some s_bc.tokens.size
    hclose : s_cl.tokens[s_bc.tokens.size]!.val.isFlowClose = true

— which is the same five readings item 265 measured firing at all 144 deaths.
`FlowBaseAnchor.gate_of_close` packages the spend; `FlowIndentStable` supplies
the indents half of the transport (8 of its 15 lemmas are applied, at 16 sites; of
the 20 `FlowBaseAnchor.*` lemmas, 8 state an indents premise and 5 discharge one
from `FlowIndentStable` in place, the rest being steps whose stability is
definitional).

So the question item 266 has to answer is not *what to build* but *what this
transport refuses to carry, and who pays*.  §6 of
`Tests/Guards/Proofs/ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.lean` answers the first half and
`scripts/carrier_price.py` the second.

## §2 The park is forced, and it is not the one in use

    carrierCore == (144, 144, 144, 144, 144, 18, 0, 90)

The anchor's four transport fields, evaluated at the death state against each
candidate park.  Against **preprocessing's** state — `below`, `held`, `ind`,
`parkFlow` — all four hold at all 144.  Against the state the step BEGAN from,
the hold resolves at **none** of them, because preprocessing's own pushes sit
between the two arrays; the stack agrees at 90 and the array never does
(`anchorProp`'s third count is 0 of 144).  There is one park and the runtime
picks it.

The existing anchor uses the other one.  `propsPark_open_gate` runs
`ParkAnchor.ofOpen` with `sc0 := sc`, whose `htok : s'.tokens = sc0.tokens.push
p` is exactly the equality that fails at every landing here.

## §3 At that park the carrier is a PASSENGER

    carrierPark == (144, 0, 144, 144, 144)

Preprocessing's cursor column **is** the open's column, at all 144.  So the
carried fact can be written over the park alone —

    sc0.indents.any (fun e => e.column == (sc0.col : Int)) = true

— with no reference to the state it is transported to, which is what makes it a
passenger: every transport lemma hands it back verbatim, the way `parkProp` is
handed back today.  At the other park the same MEMBERSHIP holds (the third
count, 144) but the column is not the park's (the second count, 0), and a field
that mentions the transported state is a premise at every step instead.  The
choice of park is the difference between the two.

## §4 What blocks the existing anchor is one field, and it covers 18 of 144

    anchorProp == (144, 18, 0, 90)

`ParkAnchor.parkProp` — "the park's last real token is a node property" — holds
at 18 of the 144 landings, the props cells alone.  It is a pure passenger: read
by the genesis (`ofOpen`) and by the spend (`dangling_eq`), handed back verbatim
by all six transport lemmas in between.  `carrierCore`'s sixth count is the
overlap from the other side: of the 144 where the transport core holds, 18 carry
`parkProp` too.

The fourth count is the unwind, and it is the same 90 that §8.1 kills.

## §5 The datum's source is preprocessing's own law

    preLaw == (198, 54, 54, 144, 144)

Over all 198 columns below a park's floor, preprocessing accepts a landing out
of flow **exactly** when its column stands on the indent stack: the 54 it
refuses are the 54 whose column stands on no level, and every one of the 144 it
accepts has one.  Both directions, because either alone is a coverage report.

That is the carrier, and it is not a field threaded through the pending-state
invariant.  It is one lemma about `scanNextToken_preprocess`, one production
over from `FlowIndentStable.preprocess_indents_of_inFlow` — and it is the
complement of the class item 265 measured as "never reach the lemma": the 54
that do not dispatch are refused *because* the column matches no level.

    slotSplit == (144, 90, 0, 90, 54, 144)

And the partition is `offersNodeSlot`, read off the token array rather than off
the gate that fired: 90 offer and die at §8.1's floor, 54 do not and die at
§9.2's dangling run, the two gates never fire together, and the hold resolves to
preprocessing's array end at all 144.  Item 265 read the same 90/54 off the
error constructor; the two agree cell for cell, which is what says
`offersNodeSlot` IS the partition and not a correlate of it.

## §6 The bill, by producers

`scripts/carrier_price.py` edits `StreamAccum.lean` and counts the DECLARATIONS
each edit breaks — item 208's reading, that a new required field makes every
application site fail on arity whether or not the field is provable there.

    CARRIER-PRICE passenger=7 heavy=7 prop=8 consumer=1 gate=1

* **7** for the anchor ring — six transport lemmas (`congr`, `congrKind`,
  `grow`, `pushClose`, `pushInert`, `pushOpen`) and the genesis, `ofOpen`.
* **8** when `parkProp` comes off instead: the same seven plus the spend,
  `dangling_eq`.
* **1** for the gate ring — `propsPark_open_gate` has exactly one caller,
  `accum_flow_open_depth0`, at two sites.
* **1** for the consumer ring — `accum_flow_open_depth0` has exactly one caller,
  `accum_step_flow`, at 17 sites.

**Nine declarations in three rings**, and no ring below the third: the core's
four fields are all derivable at the open from hypotheses
`accum_flow_open_depth0` already carries — `h_optok` gives `below` and `held`,
`h_ind'` gives `ind`, and `h_fl0` through `preprocess_preserves_flowLevel` gives
`parkFlow`.  That is COMPILED rather than read off the source
(`L4YAML/Scratch/CoreAtOpen266.lean`, deleted after the run), and it is compiled
beside a control in the same file: the same four conjuncts are provably FALSE at
a state whose token array is empty, so the positive half measures the hypotheses
and not a tautology.  Nothing has to be threaded from a producer that does not
already exist, which is the reading that separates this carrier from the ~40
fields β.5 threaded through the pending-state invariant.

**And the flip has a limit worth writing down.**  `passenger` and `heavy` state
the SAME fact two ways — over the park alone, and over the array the park's open
sits in — and they read the identical census, 13 errors in the same 7
declarations.  An arity flip counts SITES, not work: it cannot tell a passenger
from a premise.  The distinction is real and it decides the design, and the only
thing that measures it is the runtime pin in §3.

### Item 267 (2026-09-26)

Item 266 priced the carrier by producers and found the transport already in the
tree.  This item builds it.  All five of item 266's recorded deliverables
landed — the transport core split out of the park anchor, the carrier added as
its own payload, preprocessing's membership law proved, and the payload spent at
the close in both of the arms the runtime splits the family into — and the build
refuted the shape the price had assumed.

## §1 What the price got right, and the one thing it could not see

`carrier_price.py`'s `passenger` probe put the carrier on `ParkAnchor` as

    parkOpenCol : sc0.indents.any (fun e => e.column == (sc0.col : Int)) = true

— a fact about the PARK alone, which every transport lemma would carry
verbatim.  Item 266 measured that reading holding at all 144 landings
(`carrierPark`) and called the carrier a passenger on that evidence.

It is a passenger, and it is not the field.  **Both gates read the OPEN TOKEN's
own position**, not the park's cursor: §8.1's floor reports `s.tokens[o]!.pos`
and §9.2 reports `s.tokens[st]!.pos`, and §7's `runStart` says `st` IS `o` at
all 54 cells that fire §9.2, with no property in front of it at any of them.
`ParkCore.below` stops one index short of the bracket, so a payload stated over
the park's cursor cannot reach either reading.  What the build carries is the
form the `heavy` probe measured:

    openCol : sc0.indents.any
      (fun e => e.column == (s.tokens[sc0.tokens.size]!.pos.col : Int)) = true

The passenger reading is not wasted — it is what the GENESIS spends.
`ParkSlot.ofOpen` takes the membership at the park's own cursor and rewrites it
through the push, because the bracket the push writes IS that cursor's token
(§7's `parkFacts`, last count, 144 of 144).  So the two readings the arity flip
could not tell apart are both real, and they sit at the two ends of the same
lemma: one is the premise, the other is the invariant.

**What separates a passenger from a premise is the CONSUMER, not the park.**
Item 266 read the distinction off the runtime and got the right answer for the
genesis and the wrong one for the transport.  An arity flip counts sites; a
runtime pin says where a fact holds; neither says what the lemma at the far end
reads.

## §2 The split, and what an arity flip cannot price

`ParkAnchor`'s four transport fields are now `ParkCore`; `ParkAnchor` extends it
with `parkProp` alone.  Ten proofs moved onto the core — `size_le`, `size_lt`,
`grow`, `pushOpen`, `pushClose`, `ofOpen`, `congr`, `congrKind`, `pushInert`,
`rewriteKey` — and ten one-line wrappers stayed behind under the anchor's name,
so no consumer of `ParkAnchor` changed.

**The seven the flip named are the anchor's CONSTRUCTORS, and a split costs a
different set.**  `size_le` and `size_lt` construct nothing, so no added field
can break them; `rewriteKey` builds its anchor out of `congrKind` and
`pushInert` and inherits whatever they supply, so it cannot break either.  All
three have to move anyway, because the second payload needs them.  Against that,
`dangling_eq` — the eighth declaration item 266's `prop` probe named — needed
**no** repair at all: it reads the core's fields through the inherited
projection.  An arity flip prices a field ADDITION and a field DELETION; a split
is neither, and it misses in both directions.

Nothing outside those twenty declarations changed.  `FlowBaseAnchor`, the gate,
the floor and every consumer in the accumulation type-check unedited.

## §3 The carrier, and why it is a payload

    structure ParkSlot (sc0 s : ScannerState) (d : Nat) : Prop extends ParkCore … where
      openCol : …

with `ofOpen`, `grow`, `pushOpen`, `pushClose`, `congr`, `pushInert` and
`rewriteKey`.  There is no `ParkSlot.congrKind`: a kind congruence pins the two
bracket predicates and says nothing about a POSITION.  The one step that
rewrites a slot in place is the `:`'s resolution, and there `KeyFloor`'s first
conjunct puts the write strictly above the base open — which is what
`ParkSlot.rewriteKey` spends instead.

**Why it is not a core field.**  §7's `acceptedParks` walks the 378 cells of the
same family that the scanner ACCEPTS.  The open's column stands on neither
candidate park's indent stack at any of them.  A `ParkCore` that demanded the
carrier could therefore not be built where the `[96]` park builds one today, and
the split is what keeps both possible.

## §4 The carrier's source was already proved — twice

Item 266 called preprocessing's membership law "the one genuinely new scanner
lemma", one production over from `FlowIndentStable.preprocess_indents_of_inFlow`.
It is not new and it is not there.  **Item 127's
`preprocess_landing_at_level`** reads a popping landing's column off the top
entry and says that entry was on the incoming stack; **item 146's
`preprocess_indents_eq_of_no_open_level`** states the same fact
contrapositively, and in the `Array.any` form both gates read; and item 128
discharged the sentinel escape that had made the first of them conditional.

What is missing is the HYPOTHESIS CONVERSION.  Item 127's lemma takes
`h_pop : s_prep.indents ≠ sc.indents`, and what a flow open's arm holds is *the
landing is below the floor the step began with*.  Two lemmas turn the second
into the first, and they are the item's only new scanner facts:

    unwindIndents_pops        (PreprocessIndentStable §1b) the loop pops when
                              its guard holds at entry
    preprocess_pops_of_below  (StreamAccum, beside item 146's) an armed landing
                              below the incoming floor dedents

with `preprocess_landing_on_stack` a three-line corollary on top.  `h_below` is
what makes the corollary a law rather than a coverage report, and
`acceptedParks` is its control in both directions: at all 378 accepted cells its
conclusion fails, and its hypothesis fails at all 378 too.

**I built the law before reading for it.**  The first version of this item
proved the membership from scratch in `IndentStackBase` §7, where
`col_on_stack_of_unwound` re-derived line for line the arithmetic item 127
already carries.  What caught it was `IndentStackBase`'s own module docstring,
whose "what it buys" paragraph names `preprocess_landing_at_level` — read three
hours after the duplicate was written, while checking an item attribution.  Two
of this project's own rules say not to do that: §3's *read what is already
said*, and §10's *a forecast copied forward is still one measurement* — item
266's phrase named the wrong production and the wrong lemma, and this item spent
on it without a search.

    ParkSlot.underIndented_eq   underIndentedFlowValuePos? s_cl = some …pos
    ParkSlot.dangling_fires     danglingNodePos?           s_cl = some …pos

Each takes the close's own four readings, exactly as `ParkAnchor.gate` does, and
returns the gate's VERDICT rather than an equation between two verdicts: the
run-end refutation needs the gate to FIRE, not to agree.  Which spend owns a

the bracket is written — it agrees cell for cell with the same reading taken on
the park's own array — so both spends take the slot as a hypothesis about the
park rather than as a second transported field.

`dangling_fires` carries one premise its twin does not: that the run starts at
the open.  That is `runStart`'s third count, and it is why one payload serves
two gates.

### Item 268 (2026-09-26)

**PRICED — no build.**  Item 267's recorded NEXT was to WIRE the carrier:
`accum_flow_open_depth0` still spends `dropClose` at `drop_ride` because nothing
hands a `ParkSlot` to the frame the open pushes, and its P5 left the open
question in one sentence — *which lemma takes that contradiction is item 268's
measurement*.  This item measured it.  The answer costs four readings, and three
of them refute the sentence that asked for them.

**The line that makes the escape necessary.**  `drop_ride` applies `h_kpkg` at
`g = none`, and `FlowBaseAnchor none _ _` is `True` by definition, so the frame
the under-run's open pushes is UNGATED.  An ungated frame's node route is
`GateOf none → …`, which is unconditional, and an unconditional route over a
landing the scanner refuses has nothing honest to supply — which is the escape.
Everything below prices making that frame gated instead.

**§1 There are FOUR checks, not two.**  §5's `dispatchSweep` read the deaths
with no tail and found them at the END-OF-INPUT gates; its `tailSweep` read the
same 144 dying at a MID-STREAM gate as soon as a sibling line follows.  Both gates exist at
both depths, so the family dies over four named checks and not two, and
`killSite == (144, 90, 54, 90, 54)` reads the same `offersNodeSlot` partition —
**90 at §8.1's floor and 54 at §9.2's dangling run** — at each of them
(`ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun` §8).  The two pairs sum to the same 144 and split it
the same way, so what the tail moves is the DEPTH of the refusal and nothing
else.  One carrier serves all four; *two consumers* does not describe the
surface.

**§2 The two halves are not the same bill, and one of them has no bill at all.**
Resolved in the environment rather than grepped — a grep sees the name and
cannot tell a binder of the statement from a step of the proof — the
accumulation's holders read

    dn/mid=21  dn/eof=5  fv/mid=0  fv/eof=0

(`Tests/Guards/Proofs/ParkBill.lean` §5).  §9.2's mid-stream check is a
hypothesis of **twenty-one** declarations and its end-of-input twin of **five**;
**§8.1's checks are held by NONE, at either depth**.  §8.1's success is derived
exactly once, inside `scanNextToken_accum_step`, and discarded on the next line
while its twin `h_dn` is threaded into twenty-one signatures — `h_fv` occurs
three times in the accumulation's own module and all three are that one site
(the name is common in the emitter chain, which is a different variable in a
different theorem).

So the fifty-four cells that die at §9.2 have a rail that already reaches the
arm the carrier is born at, and the **ninety** that die at §8.1 — the majority —
have no holder to reach.  **And the zero is a zero in this theorem, not a zero
everywhere**: the same four names are held in the emitter-scannability chain
too, §8.1's two checks **eleven** and **fifteen** times there.  A census that
reported only the first four numbers could not tell a check nothing holds from a
check nothing mentions, so the pin carries both halves (§9: an empty check is
not a check).

**§3 What gating the frame costs** (`scripts/wire_price.py`, pinned at
`ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.expectedWirePrice`):

    WIRE-PRICE gate=49 anchor=2 route=3 eof=1

Four probes, four rings.  `gate` widens `GateOf`'s arity — who READS the frame's
gate; `anchor` adds the carrier as a third conjunct of `FlowBaseAnchor` — who
BUILDS a gated frame; `route` adds a hypothesis to `FlowBaseRoutes.value` — who
supplies and who applies the node reading; `eof` adds one to
`scanNextToken_none_stream` — who drives the end-of-input consumer.

**The asymmetry is the reading.**  Putting the carrier on the anchor costs
**two** declarations — `FlowBaseAnchor.transport`, the single funnel every
transport step goes through, and `propsPark_open_gate`, the single producer of a
gated frame — while widening the gate that reads it costs **forty-nine**.  Item
267's P5 asked whether §8.1's arm needs a new gate flavor and item 268 answers
where it goes: **a carrier-aware verdict belongs on the ROUTE (3), never on

of the premise has to be discharged.

**§4 And the carrier's source cannot be applied at its consumer.**  This is the
finding the item did not go looking for.  `preprocess_landing_on_stack` is item
267's three-line corollary, the carrier's source, and it takes
`sc.needIndentCheck = true`.  Read at the state the open's own step begins with,
over the 144:

    sourceFacts == (144, 0, 144, 144, 54, 144, 90, 54)

`(rows, the flag on the incoming state, the flag one function later, out of
flow, the landing below the incoming floor, the membership the carrier names,
the indent stack unmoved, the stack popped)`.

**The flag is false at every one of the 144 and true at every one after
`skipToContent`.**  This family crosses its break INSIDE the open's own step, so
a premise stated on the incoming state names a flag the consumer never has —
and the props park's own `PendingNode.pendingProps` field says the same thing
from the other side, carrying `sc.needIndentCheck = false` at the very arm the
carrier would be born at.  The source's other premise, the landing below the
incoming floor, holds at **54** of the 144 — exactly the dedenting half, which
is exactly §9.2's — so even restated on the state the unwind consults it reaches
at most the 54 and never the 90.  The fifth and the eighth are the same dedent
counted two ways, the premise `preprocess_pops_of_below` takes and the
conclusion it draws, so neither passes vacuously.

**And the conclusion holds at all 144.**  The fact the carrier names is true
everywhere in the family; it is the LAW's hypotheses that are unavailable, not
the fact.  The law is true and unusable rather than wrong.

**§5 The rule this item adds.**  **A law's truth and a law's applicability are
different measurements, and pinning a grid measures only the first.**  Item 267
pinned `preLaw == (198, 54, 54, 144, 144)` over the same family and scored its
P4 *confirmed, and for a stronger reason than the prediction gave* — correctly,
about the law's truth.  Nothing in that measurement looked at whether the
consumer can supply the law's premises, and here it cannot supply either of
them.  §10 already says a definition nothing has instantiated is not yet
evidence; this is its other half — **a lemma no consumer can feed is not yet a
carrier**, and the check costs one reading of its hypotheses at the state the
consumer actually holds.

### Item 269 (2026-09-26)

**The rail was refuted by the file that recommended it, and the source turned
out to be a projection.**  Item 268 left two instructions: thread §8.1's check
down to the open's arm the way §9.2's is threaded, and restate the carrier's
source on the state the unwind consults.  Measuring the first says not to build
it.  Measuring the second replaces the source's premises with ones the arm can
actually hold, and carries it to all 144 landings rather than the 54 that
dedent — at the cost of one net declaration, and the retirement of a lemma item
267 added for the form being replaced.

**§1 A rail from the open would carry a tautology.**
`railPayload == (144, 144, 144, 144, 0, 90, 144, 54)`
(`ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun` §9.1).  §8.1's check runs at the open's own step and
answers `.ok` at every one of the 144 — and the fourth component is what stops
that from passing as an artifact of the guard: the landing is ARMED at all 144,
so `scanNextToken_checkFlowValueIndent` does not short-circuit, it LOOKS.  The
fifth says what it sees: `underIndentedFlowValuePos?` reports only on a run
whose last real token is a flow CLOSE, and at the open the collection has not
been opened — **0 of 144**.  Three to five steps later the same function answers
`some` at exactly the **90**, with the flow close present at all 144 and §9.2's
reading `some` at the complementary **54**.

So threading `h_fv` from `scanNextToken_accum_step` down to
`accum_flow_open_depth0` would add two binders and three arguments carrying a
statement that is true at every landing in the family for a reason that has
nothing to do with the family.  The datum the ninety die on is not yet a fact
when the rail's head runs; a carrier is the only transport that crosses those
steps.  §5 of the same guard file had already said so in prose three items
earlier — *both gates also run at the open's own step, on a state where the
collection is not yet closed, so both say `.ok` there* — and item 268's holder
census was read without it.

**§2 The source is a projection of the state the arm is handed.**
`floorFacts == (144, 144, 0, 0, 0, 54, 90, 0)` (§9.2).  Preprocessing leaves the
top of the indent stack **at the landing's own column at all 144**, left of it
at none and right of it at none.  Those two zeros are the complement of the
first count, not a control: with the equality at every row they cannot read
anything else, and a grid that never produces the other answer reports its own
coverage.  The control is `floorControl` (§9.2a), the same grid with the open on
the park's own line, where the unwind does not run:
`floorControl == (96, 0, 96, 0, 0)`.  It reads the equality at **none** of its
96 rows and the opposite answer at **all** of them — and its fifth component
says why the two families divide where they do: `preprocess_floor_eq`'s premise
`h_le` holds at **0** of the 96, so the line separating the two answers is
exactly the line the premise draws.  The fifth component of `floorFacts` is
independent of the first and is evidence: **0** rows rest on a stack of at most
one entry, which refutes the sentinel escape `preprocess_landing_at_level`
carries, so the equality is read off a stack with a real top.

That collapses item 268's split.  The last three components partition the same
144 by the floor the step BEGAN with: **54** below it, **90** exactly at it,
**0** above — and the 90 are the ones item 268 recorded as owing a second
source.  A source that reads the floor the landing RESTS at needs no second
source and no case split: `currentIndent` IS the top entry's column, so the
membership both gates read is that entry, named.

**§3 The flag was never the premise, and the line is not either.**
`lineSource == (144, 144, 144, 144, 96, 0, 0)` (§9.3).  The line moves from the
incoming state to the landing at all 144, the indent-check flag is UP on the
state `skipToContent` hands preprocessing at all 144, and DOWN on the landing at
all 144 — the break is raised by the skip and cleared by the unwind inside the
open's own step, which is why item 268 read the flag at zero on the state the
arm holds.  The control is the same grid with the open on the park's own line:
**96** rows that reach the same dispatch with no break to cross, and the
opposite answer at every one.  So the reading is a discrimination and not a
constant — but the restated source does not use it.  The line premise would have
been a second way to say the unwind ran; the resting floor says where it
stopped, which is what the membership actually needs.

**§4 What was built and what was retired.**  Two names in, one out, and two
restated — a chain four declarations long in which each is consumed by the next.

In: `landing_on_stack_of_floor_eq` — a landing standing at its own floor stands
ON the stack, by projection, with no scanner run, no preprocessing and no
sentinel; and `preprocess_floor_eq` — preprocessing comes to rest AT the
landing's own column, the lower bound paid by the trailing-content check when
the stack popped (`preprocess_indents_or_underIndent`) and by the caller's own
bound when it did not, the upper by
`preprocess_some_ssl_comments_anyCol`'s landed disjunct.  `preprocess_landing_on_stack`
and `preprocess_pops_of_below` are restated on those two.

Out: `unwindIndents_pops` (`PreprocessIndentStable` §1b), which item 267 added
for the form being replaced and which nothing else consumed.

The premise list is the point, not its length: the form item 267 gave these two
lemmas asks for the indent-check flag on the incoming state, and §3 reads that
flag at **0 of 144** there, so no arm in this family could ever have discharged
it.  The restated form asks instead for item 147's landed disjunct **verbatim**,
so that premise is another lemma's conclusion rather than a claim about what a
consumer happens to hold, plus a bound on the landing's own column.  Whether a
given arm can supply the second is a measurement of that arm and is not made
here.

Taking the disjunct verbatim costs one branch this family never enters: its
sentinel half is discharged from `IndentStackBase.SentinelBase`, and
`floorFacts`'s fifth component reads it at **0 of 144**, so the perturbation
harness carries no row for it — a branch no input reaches cannot be shown
load-bearing, and saying so is cheaper than pretending otherwise.

Three sentences of §9's own prose were corrected in the same pass: §2 described
a premise list the restated source does not have, and two paragraphs narrated
the form being replaced instead of stating what is read.

**§5 The rule.**  **A zero in a holder census prices a rail; it does not order
one.**  Item 268 measured that no declaration of the accumulation holds §8.1's
check and read that as *build the rail*.  What that census cannot see is whether
the check, delivered, would say anything at the arm — and here it would not.
A hypothesis nothing holds and a hypothesis nothing could use are different
findings, and the second is the one that decides whether to build.  The check
costs one reading of the delivered statement at the state the consumer holds:
the same reading item 268 introduced for a law's premises, applied to its
conclusion.

is the one that can mis-attribute coverage while the gate reads 100 %.

### Item 270 (2026-09-26)

**Every premise the restated source asks for is true at every input the branch
admits, and the arm can name none of them.**  Item 269 built the source and
refused to say whether any arm could feed it — *whether a given arm can supply
the second is a measurement of that arm, not of this lemma*.  This is that
measurement, taken by ELABORATION at the three sites that spend the ride rather
than by reading the proof that reaches them.  MEASURED, no build: two
instruments, one new pinned census, one new repo script, and no proof moved.

**§1 The scope item 269 recorded has a false sentence in it.**  It said the
three arms *hand `h_kpkg none` directly and never call `propsPark_open_gate`*.
`propsPark_open_gate` resolves to exactly one call in the module, and it sits on
the path into the FIRST of the three — the props park — which obtains its
`⟨gp, h_anch_p, h_pay_p⟩` and then discards `gp` on the under-run sub-arm.  The
other two never see it.  The arm table reads that row `gate_gp = POO`.

The sentence was written from the shape of the `h_kpkg none` application without
resolving the call, which is §10's rule — a forecast copied forward is still one
measurement — turned on a record one item old.  It is also why this table is
taken at the ARM and not at the declaration: an environment census of that
gate's callers resolves to `accum_flow_open_depth0` and stops, because all three
arms live inside it.

**§2 What each arm holds.**  `ARMTABLE cells=24 paid=10 owed=14`
(`scripts/arm_price.py`, pinned at `ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.expectedArmTable`):

    hok           PPP     base                PPP     noflow_prep   PPP
    le            OOO     floor               OOO     park_col_ne0  OOO
    gate_gp       POO     sibling_floor_prep  OOO

Eight readings against three arms, each asked at the spend site — `assumption`
for the six that ask whether a type is inhabited in the local context, a bare
reference for the two that ask whether a NAME is bound there.  A cell reads PAID
only if the arm already holds the reading: a derivation is a different bill from
a binder, and this table is about binders.

**The three arms are identical on every row but one.**  "Three arms wide, not
one" is true as a population count and says nothing else: for this question the
census is one row repeated three times, and the arms differ in which park they
close rather than in what they can feed the source.

**The near-miss is a different floor.**  The arms reach `h_sep_or`, whose first
disjunct carries `h_floor_prep` — but that is
`preprocess_some_separate_at_floor`'s own `n ≤ minContentIndentOf s_prep`, not

Two readings sharing a word in prose.  And it lives in the disjunct that does
NOT take the ride: the ride is in the under-run arm, which carries `h_ur`.  The
table reads `sibling_floor_prep = OOO`, so the arms hold neither floor.

**§3 Which disjunct the genesis takes, refuted rather than read.**
`genesisFacts == (144, 144, 144, 144, 144, 90, 144)` (§10).
`preprocess_some_ssl_comments_anyCol` asserts BOTH of its arms exist, so the

that answers it.  What answers it is the stale arm's own conclusion: under
`sc.needIndentCheck = false` it concludes the line and the indent stack do not
move.  The guard holds at **144** and the line moves at **144**, so that arm is
false at every row and the landed one is what is in hand — read at the arm's
statement instead of inferred from the proof that reaches it.  Both refutations
fire with different reach: the line at all 144, the stack at the **54** that pop.

**§4 The bill is a COORDINATE, not a fact.**  The three owed readings are all
TRUE at every input the branch admits.  `genesisFacts` reads the landing out of
flow at 144, the park's own cursor column nonzero at 144 and item 147's floor at
144; item 269's `floorFacts` reads the remaining bound at 54 below the incoming
floor, 90 at it and **0** above, so `h_le` holds at all 144 too.  Nothing here
is unprovable and nothing is false.  What the arm lacks is a NAME for a position
it does not carry — `h_col02` in scope is `sp_mid2.col = 0`, the MID coordinate,
where the guard is about the park's own.

**§5 The rule.**  **A premise true at every admitted input can still be
unnameable, and the two have different prices.**  §10's three rows and item
269's floor say the facts are there; the arm table says the arm cannot say so.
That is not a starved goal in §10's sense — no datum is missing from the RUN —
it is a datum missing from the CONTEXT, and what closes it is a coordinate
carried to the arm, not an experiment and not a proof.  A census that reads
the runtime and stops would have called this branch paid.

**§6 What did not move.**  No proof moved, no runtime file was touched, and no
statement changed.  `accum_flow_open_depth0` still spends `dropClose` at

**§7 Gates and perturbations.**  The battery is 25 stages now: item 270 adds

compares its table against the Lean pin the way `wire_price.py` and

**Two stages failed on the first run for a reason that was not the tree.**  This
item's `gates.sh` was copied from item 269's with the scratchpad path
substituted, and the three axiom probes live in that directory and were not
copied, so stages 9 and 19 died at `cp` before running anything and reported

build cannot stand in for — and a reader scanning the log would have seen two
red stages among twenty-three green and filed them beside stage 7's standing
red.  **A stage that fails in its setup is indistinguishable, in the log, from a
stage that fails on its subject**, and a battery with a known-red stage in it
teaches the reader to skim exactly the column where that matters.

**Perturbations: 13 rows, 12 caught, 1 vacuous by design.**  Seven components of
`genesisFacts` move under a one-off bump; four model rows move when the state a
reading is taken on is swapped or the line reading is turned from a MOVE into a
match; and one row perturbs the arm table's INSTRUMENT rather than its pin, by
weakening the question from `assumption` to one that cannot fail — under it the
table reads `paid=19 owed=5` and the pin disagrees, which is what says the cells
are the arm's and not the harness's.

**That row took three tries, and each failure was a green reading.**  The first
weakened `assumption` to `try assumption`, which SUCCEEDS while leaving the goal
open — the module still failed, the cells still read OWED, and the row reported
a pass for a reason unrelated to its claim.  The second was correct but invisible:
the instrument's pin reader had a regex whose character class demanded two
backslashes where Lean's line continuation has one, so it found no pin, printed
`no pin` and exited — and the harness, which scored the row by the ABSENCE of a
disagreement, read that as agreement.  The reader is now a character scan with
nothing to escape, and the harness scores three ways: disagreed, agreed, or
never reached its comparison.  **A row scored by the absence of a failure reads
every early exit as a pass**, which is the same defect as the thing the row was
written to catch, one level up.

The one vacuous row is declared with its reason: swapping `sc.needIndentCheck`
for `sp.needIndentCheck` cannot move a count, because the flag is DOWN on both
states the row can name — item 268 read it at 0 of 144 on the incoming state and
item 269's `lineSource` reads it down on the landing at all 144.
`skipToContent` raises it in between, so **no two-endpoint reading can locate
the break**; §9.3's three-state reading is the one that moves.

**§8 Predictions, scored.**  Eight written before any instrument ran
(`scratchpad/l4yaml-beta5-item270/PREDICTION.md`), and this is the first item of
the run where every one of them held.

- **P1** (the recorded "never call the gate" is one-third wrong) — **CONFIRMED**,

  `POO`.
- **P2, P3** (`hok` and `base` PAID at 3 of 3) — **CONFIRMED**.
- **P4** (item 147's floor OWED at 3 of 3, with a different floor as the

- **P5** (`h_le` OWED at 3 of 3) — **CONFIRMED**.  The predicted four-premise
  table was 6 PAID and 6 OWED; it reads 6 and 6.
- **P6** (`noflow_prep` PAID 3 of 3, the park's column OWED 3 of 3) —
  **CONFIRMED**.
- **P7** (the genesis takes the landed disjunct at all 144) — **CONFIRMED**, by a
  route the prediction did not name: no predicate reads which disjunct is taken,

- **P8** (the park's column is nonzero at all 144) — **CONFIRMED**, and it was

**Eight for eight is a reading about the ITEM, not about the method.**  These
predictions were written after an orientation pass that had already read the

**§9 What is left.**  **NEXT: price the coordinate.**  The ride owes

### Item 271 (2026-09-26)

**Two of the three premises the ride owes are BRIDGES the arm can write today,
and the third is a component the splitter proves and throws away one line above
the place the arm would read it.**  Item 270 read every premise of
`preprocess_landing_on_stack` as true at every admitted input and none as
nameable inside the arm, and called the debt a coordinate.  A coordinate has a
price.  This is it, and item 268's `anchor=2` against `gate=49` does not enter:
nothing is transported.  BUILT: one library lemma, one repo script, two pinned
runtime censuses and one pinned table; one mislabel and one dangling reference
corrected in shipped instruments, and one location-parsing defect fixed in two
of them.

**§1 `h_le` is a BRIDGE, and the under-run is why.**  `WhiteRunUnderRun n
sp_mid sp_prep` is not the assertion that the landing failed to reach `n`; it
is that failure LOCATED — `j < n` spaces off a column-0 line start, then either
the run's end or a tab.  All three arms split it, refute the tab half at the
step (item 68) and spend the ride on the run-end half, where `sx = sp_prep`.
There the spaces ARE the landing, so `SIndent_col'` reads `sp_prep.col = j`,
`ScannerSurfCorr.col_eq` carries that to `s_prep.col`, and the arm's own
`IndentFloor sc n` bounds `n` by `minContentIndentOf sc = (max 0 (currentIndent
+ 1)).toNat`.  `underRunEnd_col_le_currentIndent` is those four steps.  It
transports nothing, so there is nowhere for it to ride and no ring to price.

The sentinel costs nothing either, and it costs nothing for a reason the family
confirms: a stack at its base floors the index at zero, `j < 0` is the
under-run's own refutation, and the conclusion is vacuous exactly where it would
be false.

**§2 The park's column is a bridge too, and item 270's OWED was the
instrument's answer.**  `sp_scan.col ≠ 0` is a field of every one of the three
constructors — `h_col0 : 0 < sp_scan.col` at `pendingProps` and
`pendingMapValue`, `h_col : sp_scan.col = n + 1` at `pendingBlock` — in a shape
`by assumption` cannot see, because `isDefEq` does not turn `0 < x` into
`x ≠ 0`.  Item 270 said as much in its own docstring (*a derivation is a
different bill from a binder*) and the caveat turned out to be load-bearing:
**the row was a reading of the question, not of the arm.**

**§3 What is NOT a bridge, and why it is not missing either.**  The third
premise is item 147's landed floor.  It is not in scope under any spelling, and
the reason is not that it is unproved: `preprocess_some_ssl_comments_anyCol`
proves it as the last component of its landed disjunct, behind the guard
`sp.col ≠ 0 → s_prep.inFlow = false`, and `preprocess_some_separate_at_floor`
returns `⟨sp_mid, h_ssl_col.1, h_ssl_col.2.1, h_ur, h_ltsl⟩` — dropping
`h_ssl_col.2.2` one line above the arm.  Both guards are payable at all three
arms: the first is §2's bridge, the second is item 270's `noflow_prep`, PAID.

**§4 What carrying it costs.**  `COORD-PRICE arms=pendingProps,pendingBlock,
pendingMapValue ident=diagonal le=BBB park_col_ne0=BBB floor=OOO lib=1
reach=BBB` (`scripts/coordinate_price.py`, pinned at
`ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.expectedCoordPrice`, battery stage 22b).

The arity flip — the under-run disjunct gains a component that is true
everywhere and is supplied in the splitter's own proof, so the census counts
sites that must now WRITE something rather than sites where the fact is hard —
breaks **five sites in ONE library declaration**, `accum_flow_open_depth0`.
Against item 268's `gate=49` that is the whole comparison.  **And the one is
the same fact item 270 ran into**: all three arms live inside that declaration,
which is why its table had to be taken at the ARM, and it is why a
by-declaration census of this widening cannot read three either.  A census
answering *how many declarations must change* and a census answering *how many
places must be written* are different questions here by a factor of five, and
the flip prints both.

Outside the module the flip breaks **THREE files** — and only one of them is a
consumer.  `Tests/Guards/Proofs/FlowStackFloorReal.lean` restates the
splitter's whole conclusion in an `example`, so it is a genuine destructuring
site; `HypothesisReaderCensus` and `ProducerDerivation` mention the splitter
nowhere and fail because they are environment censuses over the edited module,
which any text edit moves.  **An arity flip's tree census conflates consumers
with pins**, for the same reason item 266 recorded that such a flip counts
sites and not work: the probe reads what stops elaborating, and a pin stops
elaborating when a number changes.  So the honest bill outside the library is
one consumer and two re-pins, and `coordinate_price.py wide` prints the three
names rather than the count alone.

`reach=BBB` is the positive half: with the conjunct carried, every arm spends
it in one application — the park-column bridge for the first guard, item 270's
`noflow_prep` for the second.  So the third premise is not a proof obligation
either; it is a return value.

**§5 The two premises, read at the runtime.**  `bridgeFacts == (144, 144, 144,
144, 144)` (§11) reads `underRunEnd_col_le_currentIndent`'s two premises and
its conclusion where the proof cannot see them: preprocessing lands at the
built column at all 144, the park's index is at most the incoming top plus one
at all 144, the landing is at or left of the incoming floor at all 144, and the
incoming floor is never the sentinel.

`bridgeControl == (96, 96, 96, 0, 90)` is the boundary control, taken one
column to the RIGHT — at the park's floor, which §4 of the same file measured
as the scanner's turnover.  **Both premises still read all ninety-six and the
conclusion reads zero**, which is what says the conclusion is not an arithmetic

premise the runtime cannot show directly, `j < n`.  The fifth reading is 90, and

sentinel floors, and exactly the cells the family cannot reach, because
`floorOf "props" 0` is 0 and the under-run row is empty there.  **The lemma's
vacuous branch and the family's empty rows are the same six cells.**

**§6 A shipped instrument names the wrong arm.**  `scripts/arm_price.py`
calls the three arms `props`, `pendingBlock`, `pendingContent`.  The third is
`pendingMapValue`; `pendingContent` is a different arm of the same `cases` that
spends no ride, and §4 of the guard file had the right three names in prose
since item 264.  The table's twenty-four cells are unaffected — the labels are
printed, not measured — but a reader following the instrument to the source
would have been sent to the wrong arm.

It is caught by elaboration rather than by reading: each constructor declares a
binder the other two do not, so a probe that merely REFERS to one elaborates at
its own site and nowhere else, and the 3×3 matrix is diagonal.

**§7 The rule.**  **An instrument that asks whether a name is BOUND cannot
answer whether a datum is AVAILABLE, and the gap between the two is where a
coordinate's price actually lives.**  Item 270's table was right about what it
measured and its caveat was right about what it did not; running the second
question turned two thirds of a bill into nothing.  Reading either answer as
the other would have ordered a carrier ring — item 268 priced one at 2 and one
at 49 — for a datum with nowhere to ride.

**§8 What did not move.**  `accum_flow_open_depth0` still spends `dropClose` at
`drop_ride` at all three live arms; no runtime file was touched; no existing
statement changed.  DROP reads `SITES 2` and the β.5 fixpoint is unmoved.  The one
addition is `underRunEnd_col_le_currentIndent`, which nothing yet consumes — it
is instantiated at all three arms by the instrument and by nothing in the
library.  The pricing rule *a definition nothing has instantiated is not yet
evidence* is answered here with an elaboration rather than a promise: the
instrument applies it at all three arms and reports `le=BBB`.

**§9 Gates and perturbations.**  The battery is 26 stages now: item 271 adds
**22b COORDINATE PRICE**, which edits the source, restores it byte-identical
and compares its table against the Lean pin the way stage 22a does, plus a
final rebuild because 22b's tree probe is held out of it.  Every instrument

classified and is unchanged.

**Four census pins moved, in three waves.**  `ProducerDerivation`
(`corrHyp` 433 → 434), `HypothesisReaderCensus` and `PremiseNecessityCensus`
(`constants` +1, `decls` +1, `READ` +2, `RELAY` +4 in both), and
`NarrowingWorthCensus` (`theorems` 5274 → 5275).  They surfaced one import
layer at a time because a module that fails builds none of its dependents, and
both batteries run before the chain was clean read `PINSMOVED 36` — item 269's
under-report, reproduced one item later for the same reason.  The lane moves
are justified binder by binder in one environment rather than by the aggregate
agreeing (`Verdict271.lean`): `PROP LANES read=2 relay=4 props=6 binders=13`.

**The tree census read zero twice before it read anything, and both zeros were
green.**  `coordinate_price.py`'s wide probe reported no consumer outside the
module — and the flip provably breaks one, because
`Tests/Guards/Proofs/FlowStackFloorReal.lean` restates the splitter's whole
conclusion in an `example` and proves it by the lemma.

The cause is that the two drivers spell a location differently, and the word
`error` does not merely move within the line — it crosses the path:

    lake env lean   L4YAML/…/StreamAccum.lean:11897:69: error: Tactic `assumption` failed
    lake build      error: Tests/…/FlowStackFloorReal.lean:121:22: Tactic `rfl` failed

A pattern written for either reads nothing under the other.  The first repair
was wrong for the same reason the bug was: it made the pattern search the line
instead of anchoring it, which still demanded `: error` after the column.  Under
that repair the probe reported three FAILED MODULES and zero error locations and
printed the empty census anyway.

What settles it is neither pattern but the assertion beside them: **a build that
failed while parsing no location is a broken pattern, not an empty census**, and
the probe now raises on it.  The format was then measured rather than read — a
deliberate `example : False := by rfl` under `lake build` prints the second line
above — and the parser is exercised against both real lines, plus an `info:`
line and a `trace:` line it must reject.  `scripts/wire_price.py` carried the
same anchored pattern in its own `--wide` mode, never run in a battery; it is
fixed with it.

This is the third instrument of this run whose failure mode was a GREEN reading
(item 270 found two), and all three have one shape: **the harness could not tell
"I checked and found nothing" from "I did not check."**

**Perturbations: 19 rows, 18 caught, 1 vacuous by design.**  Five components
of `bridgeFacts` and five of `bridgeControl` move under a one-off bump; four
model rows move when the state a reading is taken on is swapped, when the index
bound loses its `+ 1`, when the conclusion is narrowed from `≤` to `<`, or when
the control is stood one column left of the park's floor; and three rows
perturb the LEMMA rather than a census — weakening `j < n` to `j ≤ n`, moving
the line start off column 0, and removing the `unfold` that lets `omega` see
`minContentIndentOf` each break the proof, so none of the three premises is
decoration.

The one vacuous row is declared with its reason: reading the conclusion against
the LANDING's floor instead of the incoming one cannot move a count, because
item 269's `floorFacts` puts preprocessing at rest at the landing's own column
at all 144 — the swapped reading is `sp.col ≤ sp.col`.  The row above it reads
the split that does separate the two states, by turning `≤` into `<`.

The instrument is perturbed once, at its question: weakening the null from
`assumption` to one that cannot fail makes every row read `P`, the table reads
`le=PPP park_col_ne0=PPP floor=PPP` and the pin disagrees — which is what says
the `B` cells are the arm's and not the harness's.  That row costs a full run
of the script and is worth exactly one.

**R4 is not parallel to R3 — it is downstream of item 64**, corrected here
2026-09-04 after measuring what the tightening costs (the diagram above used to
draw R4 as its own branch, on the strength of "nothing DEFERS to
`implicitContinue`").  That remains true and is not the constraint.  The
constraint is `entryKeyPack_of_dispatch`'s landing split
([StreamAccum.lean:13245](L4YAML/Proofs/Production/StreamAccum.lean)), which
reads `by_cases hnw : n ≤ w` and spends `valueMapRoute hnw` over
`nestedBlockMap`.  Carrying `0 < m` turns that side condition into `n < w`, so
the EQUAL-width landing loses its route and falls to the pack's `Or.inr` —
strictly enlarging the punt R3's item 65 exists to drain.  The input is
`k:⏎  :⏎  b: 2`, and the events say what it should read as instead: the parser
emits ONE inner mapping with two entries at width 2 (`=VAL :` / `=VAL :` /
`=VAL :b` / `=VAL :2`), so the honest reading closes the awaited entry with
`e-node` and CONTINUES the same `[187]` — the sibling composition item 64's
run-end half has to build anyway.  Build it once; then R4's tightening has somewhere to send the equal-width case,
and 1c and 1d can go as one session.  Items 64 and 65 LOCATED it rather than
building it — `DedentLanding` and `KeyPackPunt.dedent` — because the reading it
needs is a frame stack on the pending, which is row 19's own item.
**BUILT by item 99** (2026-09-06): the frame stack is `ResumeFrames`, the
pack's resume twin threads it, and `entryKeyPack_of_dispatch`'s dedent
branch conses at the landing's level — the equal-width case has its
somewhere.  R4 is UNBLOCKED.
**Its two halves are not the same size, measured 2026-09-07 by item 107.**  1c
stands as written.  1d does not: the equal-width landing is only one of THREE
families that reach `m = 0`, the other two being the root's own mapping and the
seq-spaces key, and `Nat`'s truncating subtraction identifies the spec's `-1`
with the spec's `0` at exactly the root's index — so the tightening is a
re-indexing of `SBlockNode`, not a side condition, and 1c and 1d are no longer
one session.  See [Item 107](#item-107-2026-09-07).
**The re-indexing LANDED 2026-09-16 (item 179)**: both pack lemmas' landing
splits read `by_cases hnw : n + 1 ≤ w` now, the equal-width landing falls to
the dedent branch item 99 built — exactly the "somewhere" this paragraph
asked for — and `nestedBlockMap`'s `n ≤ k` reads as the spec's own strict
floor at the shifted convention, so carrying `0 < m` is no longer a separate
tightening at all.  What R4 still owes is `[210]`'s narrowing itself, whose

acceptance (item 179's residual) — **the crossed-window family refuses at the

at item 181**, so `k: &x⏎a` was the only ~~prerequisite of any kind~~ RUNTIME

## Indexed-pipeline parity gap

**CLOSED 2026-08-06 — full parity.** Found 2026-08-05 from downstream
(`algctl` in `soil-moisture-workflows` parses its DPS configs with
`parseYamlWithCommentsIx`, and its `notes: >` blocks came back one byte short
of both PyYAML and our own legacy pipeline). This outranked the proof work
because `parseYamlWithCommentsIx` is the entry point consumers actually call —
it is the only one carrying `nodePositions`, so anything editing YAML in place
must use it — while every gate we had (matrix scores, round-trip corpus, the
proofs) ran through the **legacy** `TokenParser.parseYaml`.

The fix ran in three plan items: **P0** indexed the dead parity harness into
`Tests.Guards` and repaired its `agree` comparison (it compared `Except`s with
`==`, for which core has no `BEq`, so the file could not have compiled even if
it had been imported); **item 6** ported the seven legacy fixes the twin lagged
(B1/B2/B3/C1/C2/C3/E) and fixed what the new coverage found (D5 —
`needIndentCheck` after a block scalar; zero-indent block scalars via
`indentFloor`; the missing §6.7 header-newline guard); **item 7** transcribed
the six missing legacy strictness checks as read-only validator walkers plus
dispatcher/preprocess throws (tab-as-indentation in two contexts, §8.1.3
auto-detect validation, doc-markers + under-indent + tab in quoted
continuations, §6.6 comment-needs-whitespace, §6.7 header `#` glue).

The standing lesson is recorded in
[Proof-breaking code patterns](#proof-breaking-code-patterns): a probe that is
not indexed into a default target is not a probe. Full divergence analysis
(D1–D5), the per-item work-lists and the 35 block-scalar parity guards are in
git.

## Surrogate hex escapes decoded to NUL

**CLOSED 2026-08-11.** `\uD800`–`\uDFFF`, and the same code points written
`\U0000D800`, decoded to **U+0000** instead of being rejected — silent data
corruption on *accepted* input, in both pipelines, which survived a round-trip
as `a: "\0"` and put a raw control byte in the event stream.

The root cause was one guard. `parseHexEscape`
([Scanner/Scalar.lean:80](L4YAML/Scanner/Scalar.lean)) and `parseHexEscapeIx`
([Scanner/IndexedScanner.lean:512](L4YAML/Scanner/IndexedScanner.lean)) tested
`val < 0x110000`, which is strictly weaker than the precondition of the function
they then called: `Char.ofNat` is total —
`dite n.isValidChar (Char.ofNatAux n) (fun _ => '\0')` — and its else-branch
**substitutes** rather than fails. The two conditions disagree on exactly the
2048 surrogates, so every one of them took the *success* branch and decoded to
NUL with no diagnostic.

Both guards are now `Nat.isValidChar` itself, so the substituting branch is
unreachable from the scanners rather than merely unvisited. A lone surrogate is
not a Unicode scalar value and has no UTF-8 encoding, so it cannot be a
character of any scalar in the representation graph (§5.1); `[60]`/`[61]`
constrain the decoded value not at all, which is the spec's gap, but §5.1
settles it for a conforming processor. Measured after the fix: all five shapes
(including the UTF-16 pair `\uD83D\uDE00`) reject in both pipelines, and
U+D7FF / U+E000 / U+10FFFF / `\x41` still decode — the guard is a hole in the
code-point line, not a ceiling.

**The proof-side claim asserting this could not happen was also false**, and its
shape is the reusable part.
[Proofs/Errors/EscapeResolution.lean](L4YAML/Proofs/Errors/EscapeResolution.lean)
§4 read: "Either the decoded code point is < 0x110000, in which case
`Char.ofNat` produces a valid Unicode char by construction, or the scanner
returns `.unicodeOutOfRange`." Both halves are true and the disjunction is still
not a safety property. The citation "produces a valid Unicode char" was doing
the work of a *faithfulness* claim while asserting only *inhabitation* — and the
lemma behind it, `char_isValidChar`, quantifies over the codomain, so `'\0'`
satisfies it. The same file simultaneously documented a U+FFFD "fallback" that
no branch implements; prose asserting two incompatible fallbacks is the tell
that neither was checked. What replaces it is checkable:
`CharClass.toNat_ofNat_of_isValidChar` — under the guard, the decoded
character's code point **is** the requested value — carried by the indexed twin
as a conjunct of `parseHexEscapeIx_decoded`.

Pins: `Tests/Reflections/SurrogateEscapeRejected.lean` (five rejections and four
byte-exact boundary streams per pipeline, plus the `Char.ofNat 0xD800 =
Char.ofNat 0xDFFF` counterexample) and nine `#guard`s in
`Tests/Guards/Proofs/EscapeResolution.lean`. The principle is
**Reflection 642**.

**Cost, against the estimate.** The emitter was structurally immune as priced —
`escapeChar` emits hex only as `\xHH` for values ≤ 0x1F, so the three 2-digit
`native_decide` bounds re-proved verbatim under the stronger guard, restated
from `< 0x110000` to `Nat.isValidChar`. Four `simp only [h_val_lt, ↓reduceIte]`
lines in the two emitter-scannability files needed no change at all once their
bound lemmas were restated. Matrix unchanged on both instrument sets;
`run-all-tests.sh` 4439/4439; full build 954 targets, warning-free.

Two things the estimate got wrong, both cheaper than expected. The duplicate-key
question ("do collapsed surrogate keys make `duplicateKeyPolicy := .error` fire
spuriously?") is **moot**, not untested: the inputs that would collapse are now
rejected before a key is ever built. And the indexed twin needed no error
channel, because the divergence is not specific to this member — see the
residual item below.

**Residual, recorded not fixed:** the *whole* escape-error family is
message-diverse between the pipelines. `\q`, `\u12`, `\x4`, `\U0011` and
`\U00110000` all surface as `unterminatedDoubleQuoted` from the indexed caller
where legacy names the specific fault, because `parseHexEscapeIx` returns
`Option` and `processEscapeIx` has no `ScanError` channel at all. Verdict-equal
in every case, invisible to the matrix (no suite case carries a malformed
escape). Filed under [Other open items](#other-open-items); giving the indexed
escape path an error channel is a self-contained piece of work whose real cost
is `parseHexEscapeIx`'s `Option` being load-bearing for
`parseHexEscapeIx_offset_monotonic`.

## Grammar completeness plan

*(was `GRAMMAR_COMPLETENESS_PLAN.md`, itself formerly `VERSION-0.4.8.md`;
consolidated into this file 2026-08-01. Completed steps are recorded here as
closure records only — the blow-by-blow progress history is in git.)*

**Goal:** prove that syntactic acceptance by `parseYaml` and membership in the
YAML 1.2.2 surface language are the same predicate, and close the biconditional
that says so.

**The biconditional this plan was written around is FALSE as stated** (recorded
2026-09-28, from an independent audit of `main` at `16562a7` by Heath Sanchez of
[Metalogic Labs](https://metalogiclabs.xyz/)):

```lean
theorem parse_iff_grammar (input : String) :   -- ~~REFUTED — do not attempt~~
    (∃ docs, parseYaml input = .ok docs) ↔ InYamlLanguage input
```

- **Forward** (v0.4.6, proven): `parseYaml input = .ok docs → InYamlLanguage input`.
  This direction stands and is unaffected.
- **Converse**: `InYamlLanguage input → ∃ docs, parseYaml input = .ok docs` — **false**,
  and false for two independent reasons that price differently.

**Reason 1 — over-approximation, repairable by narrowing.** `InYamlLanguage`
derives strings the runtime rejects because a production is looser than the
spec: `scannerDrop` (row 12), `implicitContinue` (row 19), and the fifth and
sixth found by the audit, `[82] l-directive` and `[162] c-b-block-header` (see
[The over-approximation problem](#the-over-approximation-problem)).  Each is
closed by tightening the production, and that is what rows 12 and 19 do.
Measured on this branch: `%YAML .2⏎---⏎a` is derivable and
`parseYaml` answers `unexpected content after directive at line 0, column 8`.

**Reason 2 — a layer the surface language cannot address, NOT repairable by
narrowing.** `parseYaml` enforces per-document conditions that are not
syntactic, and the surface language has no vocabulary for them: every relation
in `L4YAML/Surface/` is `SurfPos → SurfPos → Prop` with **no environment
parameter anywhere**, so `InYamlLanguage` cannot STATE the condition at any
tightness.  Measured on this branch with `lake exe tryparse`:

| input | `InYamlLanguage` | `parseYaml` |
|---|---|---|
| `*x` | derivable | `undefined alias '*x' … no preceding '&x' anchor in this document (§7.1)` |
| `!h!x` | derivable | `undeclared tag handle '!h!' … use %TAG directive to declare it (§6.8.2.2)` |

No narrowing of any production removes these: the anchor that would make `*x`
legal is a fact about *what came before it in the same document*, and the
surface relations cannot see it.  This is a change of LAYER.

**The corrected target** (chosen 2026-09-27 from the two shapes the audit
proposed; this is its "option 2", which keeps the existing load semantics):

```lean
-- SHAPE ONLY — neither predicate is defined yet; see step 5a.
theorem parse_iff_grammar (input : String) :
    (∃ docs, parseYaml input = .ok docs)
      ↔ ExactSurfaceLanguage input ∧ SerializationWellFormed input
```

`ExactSurfaceLanguage` is `InYamlLanguage` with reasons 1's over-approximations
closed — the work rows 12 and 19 already describe, plus the audit's fifth and
sixth.  `SerializationWellFormed` is new and carries reason 2: anchor/alias
ordering and tag-handle declaration state, per document.  **Nothing defines it
yet, and nothing proves the shape above**; it is recorded as the target, not as
an achievement.  The alternative shape the audit offered — a syntax-only
capstone with the stateful conditions kept out of the statement entirely — was
not chosen, because it would stop advertising what `parseYaml` actually
enforces.
